programme.title: Gàrraidhean Mòra na h-Alba
programme.desc:
Green-fingered Murdo Macdonald visits some of the country’s most important gardens to explore their design, plant-life, setting and history.
Murdo is in Ardkinglas on the banks of Loch Fyne in Argyll. In the House Gardens, he finds out about the model railway that used to run along the lochside, and wanders around the azaleas which are bursting with colour in the Ladies’ Garden. He walks up to the Old Mill by the river, then explores the champion trees and rhododendron collection in the Woodland Garden.
Roddy Maclean talks about the folklore associated with bluebells and Dr Mark Newman from the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh tells us more about the process of hybridising rhododendrons.
Tha gàirneilear sgileil, Murchadh Dòmhnallach, a’ tadhal air cuid de ghàrraidhean mòra na h-Alba, a’coimhead air an cruth, na tha fàs unnta agus an eachdraidh.
Sa phrògram seo tha Murchadh a’tadhal air Àrd Chonghlais air bruach Loch Fìne ann an Earra-Ghaidheal. Ann an Gàrradh an Taighe cluinnidh e mun mheanbh-rèile a b’àbhaist a bhi ruith ri taobh an locha, agus gabhaidh e cuairt a-measg a h-uile dath azalea ann an Gàrradh nam Ban. Ruigidh e an t-Seann Mhuilleann ri taobh na h-aibhne, mus tèid e choimhead nan sàr-chraobh agus na rhododendron ann an Gàrradh na Coille.
Bruidhnidh Ruairidh MacIlleathain air a’bheul-aithris timchioll air bròg-na-cuthaige, agus cluinnidh sinn barrachd bhon Oll. Mark Newman bho Ghàrradh Luibheanach Rìoghail Dhùn-Èidinn, mu tar-ghineadh nan rhododendron.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Murdo Macdonald Producer - Julie McCrone.

programme.title: Cuirm aig Celtic
programme.desc:
Ceòl is còmhradh bho cuirm shònraichte le Sian aig Celtic Connections. Anns a’ buidheann Ghàidhlig Albannach, tha triùir dhen na seinneadairean Gàidhlig as fheàrr – Eilidh NicCarmaig, Ceitlin Lilidh & Ellen NicDhòmhnaill – le luchd-ciùil eile nan cois gus an dàrna clàr aca a thaisbeanadh beò ann an dòigh nach cualas roimhe. Air a lìbhrigeadh le Megan NicGill-Fhaolain.
Music and conversation from Sian’s concert at Celtic Connections to celebrate the release of their second album. The Scottish Gaelic folk group comprises three of today’s top Gaelic singers - Eilidh Cormack, Ceitlin Lilidh and Ellen MacDonald - who are joined by an extended line-up of musicians to perform the album live as never before. Presented by Megan MacLellan.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Presenter - Megan Maclellan Production Manager - Gillian MacLean Executive Producer - Alasdair MacCuish.

programme.title: An Geam Àlainn
programme.desc:
Ball-coise nam ban ann an Alba bho shealladh luchd-cluiche, leithid an deugaire Osla, sgiobaidhean, leithid Caley Thistle Inbhir Nis agus sgioba WIIGA, luchd-leantainn & eòlaichean. Nì am prògram aithriseach foillseachadh cuid de na sgeulachdan iongantach a tha a’ nochdadh agus mar a tha a’ gheama a sìor dhol am meud airson cluicheadairean an latha an-duigh. Le agallamhan bho luchd-leantainn mar Màiri Anna Chaimbeul, Seòna Nic’Ill’Fhionndaig agus an sgrìobhaiche-spòrs Ailig O’Henley. Coinnichidh sinn ri feadhainn eile a thug buaidh air an spòrs, leithid an dithis a stèidhich Glasgow City F.C. , Laura Montgomery and Carol Anne Stewart, agus Fiona McIntyre, ceannard an SWPL, a bha mar mheadhan air cruth a chur air structar a’ gheama a tha againn an-diugh. Catrìona NicNèill ag aithris.
Women’s football in Scotland seen through the eyes of players, including teenager Osla; teams including Inverness Caledonian Thistle and the WIIGA squad, as well as fans and experts. The documentary reveals some of the extraordinary stories within the game and how it has evolved for the players of today, with contributions from fans Mary Ann Campbell, Seona McClintock and sportswriter Alex O’Henley.
We also meet influential figures such as Glasgow City FC founders Laura Montgomery and Carol Anne Stewart, and SWPL chief Fiona McIntyre, who were instrumental in shaping football’s modern framework. Narrated by Carrie MacNeil.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Narrator - Carrie MacNeil Executive Producer - Alasdair MacCuish Director - Iain Macleod Producer - Ewan Duncan Production Manager - Gillian MacLean.

programme.title: Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean/Wild Senses
programme.desc:
’S caomh leinn a bhith smaoineachadh gu bheil eòlas againn air an t-saoghal timcheall oirnn, ach dè ma tha sinn dìreach a’ faicinn pàirt dheth? Tha Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean a’ toirt cuireadh dhuinn coiseachd, snàmh agus leum am measg nam beathaichean agus an saoghal aca a thuigsinn nan àrainneachd fhèin.
Thairis air ceithir eapasodan iongantach, tha sinn ag ionnsachadh mu chiad-fàthan cumhachdach nam beathaichean, bho fradharc buileach mionaideach gu iasg a tha a’ blasad len craiceann. Faic mar a tha tìgearan gan cleith fhèin le bhith a’ cleachdadh an dath orains, mar a tha leumadairean a’ seòladh a’ chuain le echo-location, mathain-nighe a’ dèanamh an slighe le spògan air leth faireachail, agus tha fiù ’s craobhan a’ cur a-mach rabhaidhean ceimigeach.
Tha Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean a’ taisbeanadh taobhan falaichte de nàdar - cailèideascop de chiad-fàthan nach eil sinn ach air tòiseachadh a’ tuigsinn.
We like to think we know the world around us, but what if we’re only seeing part of the picture? This is an invitation for you to walk, swim, or leap in someone else’s paws, fins, or wings - and experience life from a wild perspective.
Across the series, we uncover animal super-senses, from high-resolution vision to fish that taste with their skin. Discover how tigers turn orange into camouflage, dolphins navigate the deep using echo-location, raccoons feel their way with hyper-sensitive paws, and even trees send out chemical alarms.
Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles Narrator - Annella MacLeod Executive Producer - Alasdair Fraser Producer - Seumas Mactaggart Editor - Innes Macleod.

programme.title: Skipinnish Aig A' Chaisteal
programme.desc:
Skipinnish le December ann an cuideachd na mìltean de luchd-leantainn aig cuirm-chiùil a’ comharrachadh 25 bliadhna de Skipinnish, bho Chaisteal Dhùn Èideann.
Skipinnish perform December in front of thousands of fans at a concert celebrating 25 years of the band, from Edinburgh Castle. Executive Producer - Alasdair McCuish Musician - Angus MacPhail Production Manager - Gillian MacLean.

programme.title: Skerryvore Aig Caisteal Floors
programme.desc:
Prògram sònraichte a’ comharrachadh 20 bliadhna de Skerryvore. Chùm an còmhlan ainmeil Albannach cuirm shònraichte do nam mìltean de luchd-leantainn ann an àrainn àlainn Caisteal Floors sna Crìochan. Le agallamhan leis a’ chòmhlan is caraidean agus le criomagan bhon chonsairt.
A special programme to celebrate 20 years of Skerryvore. The legendary Scottish band performed an anniversary show to thousands of fans in the spectacular surroundings of Floors Castle in the Scottish Borders. Featuring interviews with band members and friends, plus concert highlights.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Executive Producer - Alasdair MacCuish Production Manager - Gillian MacLean Producer - Ewan Duncan.

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc:
Ann an turas sgoinneil eile, tha Hari a' dol air tòir 'map'. Tha e a' lorg scutair agus frith-rathad fhad's a tha e ga lorg, ach am bi aige air 'map' fhaighinn agus faighinn a-mach dè tha e a' dèanamh?
In another 'aba-doo-be-dee' adventure, Hari goes in search of a map. He comes across a scooter and a pathway as he explores the area, but will he be able to find out what a map looks like and what it does?

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.sub-title: Cha fhreagair mo chù mi!/My dog won’t talk to me ║ Peicein/PetitS1E13/26
programme.desc:
Tha Teàrlach a’ faireachdainn tinn is chan eil e airson cluich. Tha Peicein agus a charaidean a’ feuchainn ri bruidhinn ris, tha iad a’ teagasg an cànan fhèin dha, is a’ feuchainn ri cainnt nan con ionnsachadh iad fhèin.
Tadeo is feeling sick and doesn't want to play. Petit and his friends try to communicate with him, teaching Tadeo human language and trying to learn dog talk themselves. Various - Linda MacLeod Various - Kim Carnie Various - Calum MacDonald Various - Calum MacAmhlaigh Various - Eoghan MacDonald Producer - Linda MacLeod Executive Producer - Bill MacLeod Editor - Chas Chalmers Production Company - Solus Productions.

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.sub-title: A’ Lorg nam Boga-bogadach/The Poc-Poc Hunt ║ CleasanAtaidh&Tilidh/TheAdventures/Abney&TealS1E10/52
programme.desc:
‘S e latha socair a th’ ann air an eilean, latha math airson a bhith dìomhain. Tha Àtaidh, Tilidh agus Nìp a’ crochadh hamag, is tha tòrr spòrs aca a’ feuchainn ri faighinn oirre. Tha na Boga-bogadaich a’ feuchainn ri faighinn oirre cuideachd, ach tha iad air an caith suas dhan adhar is a’ dol a-mach à sealladh. Càite an deach iad? Tha Àtaidh, Tilidh agus Nìp a’ falbh a’ lorg nam Boga-bogadach.
It is a lazy day on the Island. Abney, Teal and Neep put up a hammock and have a great time trying to get into it. The Poc-Pocs join in the fun but are thrown up into the air and disappear. Where have they gone? Abney, Teal and Neep go on a Poc-Poc hunt. Teal - Linda MacLeod Abney - Tony Kearney Producer - Linda MacLeod Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Editor - Chas Chalmers Production Company - Solus Productions.

programme.title: Pompon Am Mathan Beag/Pompon Little Bear
programme.desc:
Nuair a tha Pompon a’ faireachdainn nach eil sìon a' dol ceart dha, tha Dadaidh a' sealltainn dòigh dha air rudan a chur ceart!
When Pompon feels that nothing is going right for him, Dadaidh shows him a way to sort things out! Pompon - Lana Beaton Rita/Tia - Mischa Macpherson Seòras - Calum MacKinnon Siùsaidh - Rebecca MacLennan Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Producer - Mairi Macleod Editor - Phil Reed.

programme.title: Sionnach agus Maigheach (Fox & Hare)
programme.desc:
Tha Sionnach brònach nuair a chì e gun fheàrr le Maigheach a bhith a’ leughadh leabhar seach a bhith còmhla ris-san. Tha Tosg a’ moladh dhà e fhèin a chur ann an riochd ridire gaisgeil airson aire Maighich fhaighinn air ais. Tha an dithis aca a’ togail dràgon leis a’ bheachd gum faigh Sionnach buaidh air an dràgon, agus gun dearbh e a luach do Mhaigheach.
When Hare would rather read her big book of fairytales than hang out with Fox, he fears he’s not exciting enough. According to Tusk, only by becoming a brave knight will Fox be able to prove the opposite is true. The two decide to build a dragon so Fox can beat it in battle and prove his worth to Hare. Director - Linda MacLeod Production Company - Solus Productions.

programme.title: SpongeBob
programme.sub-title: Sgrùdadh Slàinte ║ S1E4/26. The Check-Up ║ S1E4/26
programme.desc: Tha Mgr. Crùbag air a chlisgeadh mun sgrùdadh slàinte aige. Mr Krabs is too scared to get his physical.

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc:
Ged a tha na saor-làithean air tòiseachadh do sgoilearan Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche, tha latha a bharrachd aig an luchd-teagaisg airson beagan trèanaidh. Tha an t-eòlaiche-inntinn Sìleas Stern os cionn sheiseanan gus sìth agus càirdeas a stèidheachadh am measg an luchd-obrach.
Although the holidays have started for the pupils of Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche, the teachers have an in-service day. Mr Mackle is keen to establish better relationships between his staff and has invited psychologist Sìleas Stern to run team building sessions that he hopes will bring peace and harmony.

programme.title: Calum: Cogadh nan Comhlan
programme.desc:
Tha Calum airson a chòmhlann aige a thoirt à Glaschu dhan Òban airson blàr mòr ciùil a tha dol aig a' Mhòd Nàiseanta Rìoghail. Ach, le tòrr fharpaisean agus gainead tìde, chan eil cùisean a' dol mar bu chòir. Leis nach eil e furasda còmhlan a làimhseachadh aig na h-amannan as fheàrr, saoil ciamar a thèid dhaibh leis na dùbhlain mhòra a th' air thoiseach orra...
Calum aims to take his band from Glasgow to Oban for a major musical battle at the Royal National Mòd. However, with numerous competitions and time constraints, things aren't going according to plan. Managing a band is never easy even in the best of times - how will they cope with the significant challenges that lie ahead? Director - Donald Ewen MacKinnon Executive Producer - Bill MacLeod.

programme.title: Oidhche Shamhna CBBC ALBA
programme.desc:
Tanith Rothach le taghadh a tha eagalach fhèin math airson Oidhche Shamhna, le slaidhm, braimeannan agus taibhse no dhà cuideachd!
Tanith Munro introduces some frighteningly good highlights for Halloween, with slime, farts and a ghost or two!

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Rurachd (Foraging)
programme.desc:
Màiri Anna NicUalraig agus Liusaidh Cooke – An Còcaire Fiadhain – a’ rùrachd airson tairbheartas nàdair. Tha an ditches aig an taigh as t-fhoghar, a’ coimhead air an lath dhen bhliadhna far am bithear a’ trusadh airson nam preasachan a chumas biadh ri duine tron gheamhradh. Tha Màiri Anna is Liusaidh a’ giollachd dhuircean daraich airson flùr a dhèanamh dhiubh, tha iad a’ lorg balagan fiaclach ann an Loch Aills, agus tha iad a’ dèanamh air Ceann a’ Ghiùthsaich air thòir air measan cùbhraidh nan aiteann. Agus tha iad a’ gabhail cuairt a dh’Eilean Èisdeil, feuch an trus iad sìol milis, blasta Lus nam Buadh agus far a bheil iad a’ beachdachadh air deifir bhuill de theaghlach phlanntrais nan curran.
Mary Ann Kennedy and Lucy Cooke – The Wild Cooke – forage for nature’s bounty. The two are at home in autumn, looking at the half of the year where cupboards are stocked to see through the winter. Mary Ann and Lucy process acorns to make flour, forage for hedgehog mushrooms in Lochalsh, and head for Kingussie in search of fragrant juniper berries. They also take a trip to Easdale island to harvest sweet and tasty angelica seeds and consider the different members of the carrot plant family.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Faodail
programme.desc:
Tha Tasglann Fhilm Faodail a’ tarraing aire gu filmichean dhùthchasach Innse Gall bho na 1930an gu na 80an, a bha caillte ach a-nis glèidhte don ghinealach ri teachd. Tha bhana Cinema Sgìre Leantainneach a’ siubhal nan eilean, a’ taisbeanadh fhilmichean sna sgìrean ionadail, le cothrom am faicinn air-loidhne air feadh an t-saoghail. Cuirear aithris bheairteach ùr riutha, a’ buntainn ris a’ Ghàidhealtachd, airson luchd-amhairc an là an-diugh.
The Faodail Film Archive celebrates lost indigenous film collections from the 1930s-1980s in the Outer Hebrides, preserving the archive for future generations. The Cinema Sgìre Continuing mobile cinema van travels the islands showcasing footage to local communities, making them accessible globally online and adding rich new narratives relevant to the Gàidhealtachd for contemporary audiences.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Narrator - Kirsty Macdonald Producer - Andy Mackinnon Production Manager - Eilidh Johnson Executive Producer - Margaret Cameron.

programme.title: Samhradh air Sàl
programme.desc:
Angus Mackay is joined by close friend Finlay Macleod from Scalpay for the final fishing trip of the season. With summer fading, the environment looks very different as the purple heather really comes to the fore.
Tracked by the golden eagle, they sail north to the hamlet of Calbost to take advantage of the shelter offered by its bay on a less than optimal day. As the duo fish in the bay, they ponder the extremes of the sea - its matchless beauty and its mortal danger.
Anns a’ phrògram mu dheireadh san t-sreath, tha Fionnlagh MacLeòid à Sgalpaigh, còmhla ri Aonghas airson an turas iasgaich mu dheireadh den t-seusan. Leis an samhradh a’ tighinn gu crìoch, tha an àrainneachd a’ coimhead gu math eadar-dhealaichte, ‘s am fraoch purpaidh a’ tighinn am follais. Air an leantainn le iolaire-bhuidhe, seòlaidh iad gu tuath, gu Calbost gus beagan fasgadh fhaighinn sa bhàgh, air latha meadhanach grod. Fhad ’s a tha iad ag iasgach, tha iad a’ meòrachadh air an dà chuid cunnart agus bòidhchead na mara.

programme.title: Seirm
programme.desc:
Highlights and previously unseen performances, featuring Mairi McGillivary, Ciaran Ryan and Fara.
Roghainn fon sreath ciùil comhla ri Màiri Nicillebhrath, Ciaran Ryan and Fara. Presenter - Mary Ann Kennedy Executive Producer - Alasdair MacCuish Director - John Smith Producer - Iain Macleod.

programme.title: Fonn mo Bheatha
programme.desc:
Music and chat programme presented by Cathy Ann MacPhee, with guest Calum Alex MacMillan.
Ceòl agus còmhradh le Cathy Ann Nic a Phi còmhla ri Calum Ailig MacMhaolain.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Presenter - Cathy-Ann MacPhee.

programme.title: Gàrraidhean Mòra na h-Alba
programme.desc:
Green-fingered Murdo Macdonald visits some of the country’s most important gardens to explore their design, plant-life, setting and history.
Murdo is in Ardkinglas on the banks of Loch Fyne in Argyll. In the House Gardens, he finds out about the model railway that used to run along the lochside, and wanders around the azaleas which are bursting with colour in the Ladies’ Garden. He walks up to the Old Mill by the river, then explores the champion trees and rhododendron collection in the Woodland Garden.
Roddy Maclean talks about the folklore associated with bluebells and Dr Mark Newman from the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh tells us more about the process of hybridising rhododendrons.
Tha gàirneilear sgileil, Murchadh Dòmhnallach, a’ tadhal air cuid de ghàrraidhean mòra na h-Alba, a’coimhead air an cruth, na tha fàs unnta agus an eachdraidh.
Sa phrògram seo tha Murchadh a’tadhal air Àrd Chonghlais air bruach Loch Fìne ann an Earra-Ghaidheal. Ann an Gàrradh an Taighe cluinnidh e mun mheanbh-rèile a b’àbhaist a bhi ruith ri taobh an locha, agus gabhaidh e cuairt a-measg a h-uile dath azalea ann an Gàrradh nam Ban. Ruigidh e an t-Seann Mhuilleann ri taobh na h-aibhne, mus tèid e choimhead nan sàr-chraobh agus na rhododendron ann an Gàrradh na Coille.
Bruidhnidh Ruairidh MacIlleathain air a’bheul-aithris timchioll air bròg-na-cuthaige, agus cluinnidh sinn barrachd bhon Oll. Mark Newman bho Ghàrradh Luibheanach Rìoghail Dhùn-Èidinn, mu tar-ghineadh nan rhododendron.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Murdo Macdonald Producer - Julie McCrone.

programme.title: Dàna
Scotland's Wild Side
programme.sub-title: Am Monadh Ruadh/Cairngorms ║ Dàna. S3. ALBAE2/4
programme.desc:
The vast landscape of the Cairngorms attracts thousands each year. Coinneach Rankin sets out on a multi-day expedition to learn why its vast mountains are a paradise for climbers, runners and so many others. Along with his partner, Coinneach races up one of the highest mountains in Scotland, undertakes a classic multi-pitch climb, and spends the night in a tiny bothy built in the 1960s.
Tàlaidh cruth-tìre aibheiseach a’ Mhonaidh Ruaidh na mìltean gach bliadhna. Cuiridh Coinneach MacFhraing aghaidh air turas grunn làithean gus tuigsinn carson a tha sreapadairean, luchd-coise agus eile cho measail air na beanntan seo.
An cuideachd deagh charaid, thèid Coinneach na dheann suas tè de na beanntan as àirde an Alba, dìreidh e slighe-sreapa fhada agus cuiridh e seachad na h-oidhche ann am bothan a thogadh ‘sna seasgadan.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Coinneach Rankin Executive Producer - Tony Kearney Executive Producer - Jim Webster Executive Producer - Calum McConnell Director - Hamish MacLeod.

programme.title: Rathad Ramsay
programme.desc:
Ramsay meets Ian Smith in the village he was brought up, before they head along one of Tiree’s most famous beaches. As they walk along the coast, Ian reflects on his youth and the people that impacted him.
Ian discusses how the Tiree music scene shaped him and brought him success as a box player, and he shares his passion for the island and his pride in setting up the only distillery in Tiree.
San treas sreath de Rathad Ramsay bidh Ramsay MacMahon a’ coinneachadh ri sàr Ghàidheil bho air feadh Alba ‘s iad a’ co-roinn sgeulachdan, cuir luach air nàdar agus a’ cnuasachadh ma beatha.
Coinnichidh Ramsay ri Iain Mac a’ Ghobhainn sa bhaile san d’rugadh e mas dèan iad air tè de na tràighean as iomraitiche ann an Tiriodh. Meòirichidh Iain air làithean òige agus na daoine bu mhotha a thug buaidh air a bheatha.
Leis cho cudromach ‘s a tha ceòl air eilean Thiriodh, innsidh Iain man bhuaidh a bh’aige seo air fhèin agus mar a chuidich e a bhith cho soirbheachail le cluich a’ bhogsa. Bidh an dà chuid a mheas air an eilean agus a mhoit man aon taigh-stàile san eilean fhaighinn stèidhichte follaiseach.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Ramsay MacMahon Series Producer - Robyn Low Editor - Mairead Morrison.

programme.title: Ceol Sith
programme.desc:
Thigibh air turas a-steach gu saoghal shìthichean agus creutairean os-nadarra eile. Air chuairt ann an Alba, tha Ingrid NicEunraig a’ cluinntinn beul-aithris agus sgeulachdan a tha fhathast beo. Anns a’ program sònraichte seo, tha Ingrid a’ tòiseachadh ann an Loch Abar far a bheil mòran stòraidhean mar seo air maireachdainn.
As dèidh sin tha I a’ cluinntinn sgeulachdan nas tradisteanta anns an Eilean Sgiathanach. Tha I cuideachd a’ cluinntinn sgeulachd bhampire ann an Glaschu agus mu bheathaichean bhon uisge ann an Uibhist, mu maighidinn-mara agus each-uisge. Tha a cuid-siubhal ga brosnachach gus ceòl ùr a sgriobhadh agus a chluich ann an cuid de na h-àiteachan as drùidhteach san dùthaich. Air aon làimh ’s eeàlachas a th’anns a’ phrògram seo ach aig an aon àm, tha e a’ toirt dhuinn sealladh air spiorad mac an duine.
This is a thrilling journey into the world of fairies and folklore. Ingrid Henderson presents a tour around Scotland’s rich mythical worlds and composes music to bring them back to life.
Ingrid starts on her home turf in Lochaber, where these stories are very much alive, and then heads to Skye with its traditional fairy stories. She also hears about a terrifying creature in Glasgow - the Gorbals vampire - and talks to people in Uist about watery creatures such as mermaids and kelpies.
As she travels, Ingrid draws inspiration from the stories to create and perform specially composed music for the programme in stunning locations around the country. On the one hand, this documentary is pure escapism, but it also gives us insight into the human spirit.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Ingrid Henderson Executive Producer - Maureen MacLeod Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - Annie Cheape.

programme.title: Ath-thogail Notre-Dame/Rebuilding Notre-Dame
programme.desc:
Air a togail san dàrna linn deug ann am meadhan Paris (air an Île de la Cité), aig aon àm b' e Notre-Dame a' chathair-eaglais a b' àirde air thalamh. Tha an t-soitheach aibhseach cloiche seo a' riochdachadh ailtireachd Gotach. Ach tha a seasmhachd a-nise ann an cunnart.
Rinn an teine milleadh air cothromachd an togalaich. Chaidh am mullach a sgrios, còmhla ris a' chliath iongantaich fiodha seo – air a dèanamh de mhìle craobh daraich – 's chaidh a losgadh san teine. Ach fhathast cha do thuit Notre-Dame. Dè as coireach gu bheil i cho làidir? Am measg an sprùillich chaidh iomadh ceangal meatailt a lorg, cuid de mheud iongantach. An robh iad nam pàirt dhen chiad dhealbhadh no nach robh? An gabhadh e a bhith gun do dh'fhuiling Notre-Dame trioblaidean structarail eile tro na linntean?
Leanaidh sinn gu dlùth an luchd-saidheans is na h-ailtirean is iad a' sgrùdadh a' chliath iongantach fiodha is meatailt a bh' air cùl na cloiche. Le cuideachadh bho dhealbhan 3D agus ath-achdachaidhean gheibh sinn tuigse air toiseach an togalaich mhòrail seo.
Built in the 12th century in the centre of Paris (on Île de la Cité), Notre-Dame was once the world's highest cathedral. This gigantic stone structure is the very essence of Gothic architecture. But today, its stability is compromised.
The 2019 fire greatly damaged the building's structure. Its roof was completely destroyed, as well as its incredible wooden frame, made of a thousand oaks, which was swallowed by the flames. Still, Notre-Dame did not collapse. What are the secrets of this exceptional strength? Amongst the wreckage, many metal fasteners were found, some of incredible size. Were they part of the original design or not? Is it possible that Notre-Dame encountered other structural problems throughout the centuries?
We closely follow scientists and architects as they study the impressive skeleton of wood and metal which hid behind the stone. Supported by 3D animations as well as re-enactments, their interventions allow us to grasp the genesis of this monumental structure.
Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles. Narrator - Anna Murray Producer - Seumas Mactaggart Executive Producer - Shona Henderson Executive Producer - Calum McConnell Editor - Innes Macleod.

programme.title: Abigail
programme.sub-title: Brot Coiridh le Leantail is Leigeas ║ AiganTaighleE6/12
programme.desc:
'S e th' ann am Brot fìor bhlast' de Choiridh leantail, ach lòn sònraicht' nach dìochuimhnich thu ann an cabhaig.
An extremely delicious curried lentil soup is a special lunch which you won't forget in a hurry.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Abigail Maciver Producer - Kenneth Stewart Production Manager - Mairi Macleod Executive Producer - Rachel Ellen Mackay.

programme.title: An Geam Àlainn
programme.desc:
Ball-coise nam ban ann an Alba bho shealladh luchd-cluiche, leithid an deugaire Osla, sgiobaidhean, leithid Caley Thistle Inbhir Nis agus sgioba WIIGA, luchd-leantainn & eòlaichean. Nì am prògram aithriseach foillseachadh cuid de na sgeulachdan iongantach a tha a’ nochdadh agus mar a tha a’ gheama a sìor dhol am meud airson cluicheadairean an latha an-duigh. Le agallamhan bho luchd-leantainn mar Màiri Anna Chaimbeul, Seòna Nic’Ill’Fhionndaig agus an sgrìobhaiche-spòrs Ailig O’Henley. Coinnichidh sinn ri feadhainn eile a thug buaidh air an spòrs, leithid an dithis a stèidhich Glasgow City F.C. , Laura Montgomery and Carol Anne Stewart, agus Fiona McIntyre, ceannard an SWPL, a bha mar mheadhan air cruth a chur air structar a’ gheama a tha againn an-diugh. Catrìona NicNèill ag aithris.
Women’s football in Scotland seen through the eyes of players, including teenager Osla; teams including Inverness Caledonian Thistle and the WIIGA squad, as well as fans and experts. The documentary reveals some of the extraordinary stories within the game and how it has evolved for the players of today, with contributions from fans Mary Ann Campbell, Seona McClintock and sportswriter Alex O’Henley.
We also meet influential figures such as Glasgow City FC founders Laura Montgomery and Carol Anne Stewart, and SWPL chief Fiona McIntyre, who were instrumental in shaping football’s modern framework. Narrated by Carrie MacNeil.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Narrator - Carrie MacNeil Executive Producer - Alasdair MacCuish Director - Iain Macleod Producer - Ewan Duncan Production Manager - Gillian MacLean.

Le Màiri Anna NicUalraig agus Alistair Heather air an àrd-ùrlar agus air cùl stèids, coinneachaidh sin ris na luchd-ciùil agus na rionnagan a shoirbhich air an oidhche. Performances from Peatbog Faeries, Mànran, Joy Dunlop, Karine Polwart & Dave Milligan, Amy Laurenson, SC & T Youth and a musical tribute to a national treasure - the late Robbie Shepherd. programme.title: Sailm nan Daoine
programme.desc:
Tha Rob MacNeacail air turas gus sailm Ghàidhlig a sheinn is a sgaoileadh. ’S e film tarraingeach is togarrach a tha seo mu chumhachd na coimhearsnachd, an teaghlaich is an seasmhachd a tha a dhìth gus cànan a chumail beò.
Thòisich Rob air na sailm a ghabhail ann an Carlops gus comharrachadh ceann-bliadhna bàs athar, am bàrd Aonghas MacNeacail. Ged a tha na seiseanan a’ còrdadh ri muinntir a’ bhaile, tha Rob ga cheasnachadh fhèin a bheil còir aige a bhith a’ teagasg nan salm. Cha do dh’ionnsaich e mar a stiùireas e an t-seinn ach o chionn ghoirid, agus cha deach a thogail san eaglais. Chan eil Rob aig tàmh is e a’ faireachdainn gum feum e falbh air turas gus cluinntinn mar a bhios na Gàidheil a’ seinn nan salm anns na coimhearsnachdan a tha a’ cumail an traidisein beò.
Bheir an turas e bho na h-Eileanan an Iar gu Corcaigh an Iar, a’ leantainn seann shlighean a bheireas ceòl is beachdan ùra gu bith.
Rob MacNeacail embarks on a mission to sing Gaelic psalms. An entertaining and heartwarming film about the power of community, family and the resilience needed to keep a language alive.
Rob started singing the psalms in his home village of Carlops to mark the anniversary of the death of his father, the poet Aonghas MacNeacail. Although the sessions are popular with locals, Rob starts to question his authority to teach the psalms, as he only learned how to precent relatively recently and didn’t grow up in the church.
As spring turns to summer, Rob starts to feel restless and decides to hit the road to reconnect with his Gaelic roots and hear how psalms are sung by Gaels in the communities that nurture the tradition. His journey takes him from the Western Isles to West Cork in Ireland, following well-trodden ancient paths that unravel threads of music and ideas along the way.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Director - Jack Archer Executive Producer - John Archer Editor - James Alcock Executive Producer - Calum McConnell Production Manager - Mhairi Valentine Production Company - Hopscotch Films.

programme.title: Alba fon Talamh/Scotland Underground
programme.desc:
In the Highlands and Islands, Calum explores the caves of Assynt, a Unesco global geopark, before travelling north to Orkney where there is a wealth of archeological underground sites. But it is also an example of the modern use of subterranean sites: oil to service the Scapa Flow naval sites was hidden underground in vast tanks beneath Wee Fea hill. The war theme continues as Calum visits a Cold War underground bunker in Inverness.
Anns a’ Ghàidhealtachd agus na h-Eileanan, bheir Calum cuairt tro uamhan Asainte, geò-pàirc cruinneil UNESCO. À sin, thèid e tuath gu Arcaibh far a bheil beartas de làraich arceòlach fon talamh, ach cuideachd eisimpleir nas ùire den fho-thalamh a chleachdadh. Fo chnoc Wee Fea, tha na tancaichean mòra a bha a’ cumail ola ri làrach a’ Chabhlaich Rìoghail ann an Scapa Flow. A’ cumail ri tèama a’ chogaidh, ann an Inbhirnis tadhlaidh Calum air buncair bho àm a’ Chogaidh Fhuair.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Rurachd (Foraging)
programme.desc:
Màiri Anna NicUalraig agus Liusaidh Cooke – An Còcaire Fiadhain – a’ rùrachd airson tairbheartas nàdair. Tha an ditches aig an taigh as t-fhoghar, a’ coimhead air an lath dhen bhliadhna far am bithear a’ trusadh airson nam preasachan a chumas biadh ri duine tron gheamhradh. Tha Màiri Anna is Liusaidh a’ giollachd dhuircean daraich airson flùr a dhèanamh dhiubh, tha iad a’ lorg balagan fiaclach ann an Loch Aills, agus tha iad a’ dèanamh air Ceann a’ Ghiùthsaich air thòir air measan cùbhraidh nan aiteann. Agus tha iad a’ gabhail cuairt a dh’Eilean Èisdeil, feuch an trus iad sìol milis, blasta Lus nam Buadh agus far a bheil iad a’ beachdachadh air deifir bhuill de theaghlach phlanntrais nan curran.
Mary Ann Kennedy and Lucy Cooke – The Wild Cooke – forage for nature’s bounty. The two are at home in autumn, looking at the half of the year where cupboards are stocked to see through the winter. Mary Ann and Lucy process acorns to make flour, forage for hedgehog mushrooms in Lochalsh, and head for Kingussie in search of fragrant juniper berries. They also take a trip to Easdale island to harvest sweet and tasty angelica seeds and consider the different members of the carrot plant family.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Ceol Sith
programme.desc:
Thigibh air turas a-steach gu saoghal shìthichean agus creutairean os-nadarra eile. Air chuairt ann an Alba, tha Ingrid NicEunraig a’ cluinntinn beul-aithris agus sgeulachdan a tha fhathast beo. Anns a’ program sònraichte seo, tha Ingrid a’ tòiseachadh ann an Loch Abar far a bheil mòran stòraidhean mar seo air maireachdainn.
As dèidh sin tha I a’ cluinntinn sgeulachdan nas tradisteanta anns an Eilean Sgiathanach. Tha I cuideachd a’ cluinntinn sgeulachd bhampire ann an Glaschu agus mu bheathaichean bhon uisge ann an Uibhist, mu maighidinn-mara agus each-uisge. Tha a cuid-siubhal ga brosnachach gus ceòl ùr a sgriobhadh agus a chluich ann an cuid de na h-àiteachan as drùidhteach san dùthaich. Air aon làimh ’s eeàlachas a th’anns a’ phrògram seo ach aig an aon àm, tha e a’ toirt dhuinn sealladh air spiorad mac an duine.
This is a thrilling journey into the world of fairies and folklore. Ingrid Henderson presents a tour around Scotland’s rich mythical worlds and composes music to bring them back to life.
Ingrid starts on her home turf in Lochaber, where these stories are very much alive, and then heads to Skye with its traditional fairy stories. She also hears about a terrifying creature in Glasgow - the Gorbals vampire - and talks to people in Uist about watery creatures such as mermaids and kelpies.
As she travels, Ingrid draws inspiration from the stories to create and perform specially composed music for the programme in stunning locations around the country. On the one hand, this documentary is pure escapism, but it also gives us insight into the human spirit.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Ingrid Henderson Executive Producer - Maureen MacLeod Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - Annie Cheape.

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc:
Tha sinn air ais ann an Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche airson teirm ùr. Tha tòrr air tachairt thairis air na saor-làithean. Cha robh an là in-sheirbheis cho soirbheachail `s a bha Maighstir Mackle an dùil agus tha Ms Sharpe air nochdadh sna pàipearan-naidheachd ri linn ‘s na thachair aig a’ Mhòd.

programme.title: Flix
programme.desc:

programme.title: Golf: Mun Cuairt Alba
programme.desc:
Le còrr air 550 raon-goilf tha Alba cliùiteach mar dhachaigh ghoilf. Tha an sreath 6-pàirt seo a’ gabhail turas air feadh na dùthcha gu na cùrsaichean ainmeil agus na seudan àlainn nach eil cho iomraiteach, a’ fosgladh ar sùilean gu goilf. Cluinnidh sinn bho ghoilfearan sean is òg, fireann is boireann, goilfearan dall is goilfearan ciorramach, agus bho chuid a bhios a' cosnadh beòshlaint à goilf.
An t-seachdain-sa, gabhaidh sinn sgrìob-adhair mu chuairt taghadh de raointean-goilf anns na h- Eileanan an Iar, cluinnidh sinn mu eachdraidh Aisgeirnis ann an Uibhist a Deas, tha Stuart Griffin is Hugh Ross a’ cluich goilf le aon ghàirdean agus cluinnidh sinn an sgeòil aig Club Goilf Shruighlea. Agus tha coidse proifeiseanta Keil Beveridge a’ toirt seachad comhairle na seachdaine airson dòigh-cluiche.
Scotland has over 550 golf courses and is regarded worldwide as the home of golf. This series takes us on a journey around the country to explore some of the well-known courses as well as some of its hidden gems, and opens the door to golf. We hear from golfers young and old, male and female, blind and disabled, and from those who make their living working in golf. We also capture a few tips from the professionals along the way.
In this episode, we take an aerial journey around a selection of golf courses in the Western Isles. We learn about the story of the historic golf course at Askernish in South Uist.
Stuart Griffin and Hugh Ross are one-armed golfers who compete internationally. We catch up with them playing at Stirling Golf Club. And professional coach Keil Beveridge demonstrates his weekly top playing tip.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Expert - Keil Beveridge Expert - Laura Murray Producer - Patricia Macleod Director - Scott Brown Editor - Jonny Craigmile.

Thairis air an t-sreath, bidh i a’ dèiligeadh ri facail is abairtean air measgachadh de chuspairean co-cheangailte ri gach taobh de ar beatha. Leis gun do dh’ionnsaich i fhèin, bheir Joy dhuinn briathrachas mu charaidean, an dachaigh, an teaghlach, obair agus an aimsir am measg gu leòr eile ann an dòigh a tha sìmplidh agus furasta a thuigsinn. Bidh stiùireadh ann cuideachd a thaobh a bhith a’ cleachdadh abairtean, le eisimpleirean soilleir ann an dramathan goirid.
Coinnichidh sinn luchd-ionnsachaidh èasgaidh, feadhainn a tha ag ionnsachadh as ùr agus cuid a bha fileanta agus a sguir ga cleachdadh, agus iadsan a th’ air a bhith ag ionnsachadh fad bhliadhnaichean. Agus bidh Calum MacIlleathain a’ toirt sealladh eile dhuinn air Alba is e ann an diofar àitichean air feadh na dùthcha.
Lorgar tuilleadh stuthan taic air-loidhne: www.speakgaelic.scot agus ann an sreath phodcastan a tha ri fhaighinn air BBC Sounds.

Tha Calum MacIllinnein a’ rannsachadh nam planaichean, a’ coinneachadh ri clubaichean, cluicheadairean is luchd-leantainn, is a’ faighneachd dè thèid again air ionnsachadh bho shiostam Nirribhidh.

programme.title: Trusadh
programme.sub-title: Clann a’ Mhansa An La An-De/Children of the Manse ║ S14E8/10
programme.desc:
’S e dreuchd gu math sònraichte a th’ aig ministear agus bha seo fìor gu h-àraidh anns na 60an agus na 70an. Duine foghlamaichte, anns an robh earbsa aig daoine ’s aig an robh seasamh làidir anns a’ choimhearsnachd. Ach an dùil cò ris a bha e coltach nam b’ e d’ athair a bha a’ searmonachadh anns a’ chubainn?
Tha an craoladair Cathy Nicdhòmhnaill a’ bruidhinn ri clann a’ mhansa an là an-dè, a chaidh an togail aig àm an uair a bha buaidh mhòr aig an eaglais. Tha i a’ bruidhinn ris an Urramach Iomhair Màrtainn, fear a lean ann an ceumannan athar agus a tha a-nis na mhodaràtair air Eaglais Shaor na h-Alba.
Tha i a’ faighinn facal air Jessie Mary Little, nighean an Urramaich Aonghas Mac a’ Ghobhainn, am ministear a chaidh an aghaidh bàtaichean-aiseig na Sàbaid ann an 1965, agus tha i cuideachd a’ còmhradh ri Dòmhnall Iain MacAmhlaigh, mac an urramaich Murchadh MacAmhlaigh, a tha a’ mìneachadh mar a thug creideamh buaidh làidir air a bheatha fhèin, am measg cuid eile, is iad uile ag innse sgeulachdan mu am pàrantan agus mu sheirbheisean ’s na h-òrdaighean, a’ dèanamh dealbh math de na sgìrean eaglais anns an deach an togail. A’ coimhead air ais, ciamar a tha seo air buaidh a thoirt air mar tha iad fhèin a’ coimhead air an t-saoghal?
A minister's important role was much to the fore in the 60s and 70s. A person whom people trusted, who was knowledgeable and well-educated, and who held a strong position in the community. But what was life like if your father was the one preaching in the pulpit?
Broadcaster Cathy Macdonald talks to sons and daughters of the manse, who were brought up during a time when the church had far reaching influence. She speaks to the Rev Iver Martin, who followed in his father’s footsteps and became a minister, and who is now the Moderator of the Free Church of Scotland.
Cathy chats with Jessie Mary Little, daughter of Rev Angus Smith, the well-known minister who protested against Sunday sailings in 1965 and she also talks to Donald John MacAulay, son of the Rev Murdo MacAulay, who describes how faith has had a strong influence on his life. They all share warm-hearted stories about their parents, church services and the camaraderie of communions, creating a portrait of the parishes in which they grew up.

programme.title: An Clo Mor
programme.sub-title: Meal do Naidheachd An-Diugh - Happy Birthday ║ S1E1/6
programme.desc:
It’s make or break time at the Hebridean family-run tweed mill, ‘Muileann Mhicsuain’. Time is running out for mill owner Seumas as he tries to save his business, but his corner-cutting has horrific consequences.
A dreadful accident takes place on the mill floor that endangers the life of a beloved employee, Old Mary. With the family business in jeopardy, Seumas makes a secret phone call asking for help, but who is he reaching out to and why does he have to keep it secret from his family?
Tha taghaidhean mòra air thoiseach orra aig Muileann MhicSuain, a’ mhuileann chlò Innse Gall a th’ air a ruith le teaghlach MhicSuain. Tha an ùine a’ ruith air ceannard na muilne, Seumas, agus e a’ dèanamh nas urrainn dhà gus a’ ghnìomhachas aige a shàbhaileadh – ach tha cùisean a’ tighinn gu ceann uabhasach ri linn an dòigh-obrach charach aige. Tha tubaist eagalach a’ tachairt air làr na muilne a tha a’ cur beatha tè dhen luchd-obrach, Màiri, ann an cunnart. Le gnìomhachas an teaghlaich fo imcheist, tha Seumas a’ cur a dh’iarraidh cuideachadh – ach cò dhà a tha e a’ faighneachd agus carson a dh’fheumas e a chumail bhon chòrr dhen teaghlach?
In Gaelic with English subtitles Seumas - Ewen MacKinnon Sileas - Erica Morrison Donald - Eoghan MacDonald Murdina - Emma MacLeod Mairead - Anna Murray Production Manager - Mairi MacKinnon Executive Producer - Jim Webster Executive Producer - Tony Kearney.

programme.title: Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean/Wild Senses
programme.desc:
’S caomh leinn a bhith smaoineachadh gu bheil eòlas againn air an t-saoghal timcheall oirnn, ach dè ma tha sinn dìreach a’ faicinn pàirt dheth? Tha Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean a’ toirt cuireadh dhuinn coiseachd, snàmh agus leum am measg nam beathaichean agus an saoghal aca a thuigsinn nan àrainneachd fhèin.
Thairis air ceithir eapasodan iongantach, tha sinn ag ionnsachadh mu chiad-fàthan cumhachdach nam beathaichean, bho fradharc buileach mionaideach gu iasg a tha a’ blasad len craiceann. Faic mar a tha tìgearan gan cleith fhèin le bhith a’ cleachdadh an dath orains, mar a tha leumadairean a’ seòladh a’ chuain le echo-location, mathain-nighe a’ dèanamh an slighe le spògan air leth faireachail, agus tha fiù ’s craobhan a’ cur a-mach rabhaidhean ceimigeach.
Tha Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean a’ taisbeanadh taobhan falaichte de nàdar - cailèideascop de chiad-fàthan nach eil sinn ach air tòiseachadh a’ tuigsinn.
We like to think we know the world around us, but what if we’re only seeing part of the picture? This is an invitation for you to walk, swim, or leap in someone else’s paws, fins, or wings - and experience life from a wild perspective.
Across the series, we uncover animal super-senses, from high-resolution vision to fish that taste with their skin. Discover how tigers turn orange into camouflage, dolphins navigate the deep using echo-location, raccoons feel their way with hyper-sensitive paws, and even trees send out chemical alarms.
Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles Narrator - Annella MacLeod Executive Producer - Alasdair Fraser Producer - Seumas Mactaggart Editor - Innes Macleod.

programme.desc:
Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Emma, Dave, Lee and Jodie – take on the Bridge of Lies.
One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies.
They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game.

programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc:
Four familiar faces paired with a friend or a loved one leave their luxury lifestyles at the starting line for a journey that will take them to the other side of the world and push them to the limits of their endurance. The pairs embark on a life-changing adventure - a 7,500km race from the prehistoric jungles of Borneo to the sun-baked southern tip of Australia.
Competing in this series are acclaimed singer-songwriter and musician Sam Ryder, and his best friend and tour manager, Kaz; veteran sports broadcaster Jeff Stelling and his son Matt; BRIT award-winning singer-songwriter Ella Eyre and childhood friend Nana; and influencer Princess Andre with her brother musician Junior Andre.
Stripped of their smartphones and bank cards, these household names will be tested; emotions will run high, and relationships will be transformed on an adventure that’s as challenging as it is rewarding. They will need to rely on their own resourcefulness and the kindness of strangers to reach the finish line, equipped with only a map and a budget of £26 each a day.
Their race begins in Kuching, a vibrant city in north west Malaysian Borneo and the gateway to the island's vast wilderness. From there, the teams must cross three countries and two continents, weaving through five checkpoints before reaching the finish line in Melbourne, Australia.
The teams must tackle the most formidable race yet - traversing the ancient jungles and indigenous heartlands of Borneo, navigating the Makassar Strait to Sulawesi, an island of cinematic, towering limestone cliffs, before reaching the kaleidoscopic splendour of Queensland's landscapes, from the turquoise blues of the Great Barrier Reef to the arid, expansive orange of the outback. Finally, they will thread through sprawling Sydney before reaching the finish line on the southern tip of Australia.
Musician Sam and tour manager Kaz embrace an unexpected start to the race and dive straight in, relishing the chance to revisit the early days of their friendship when roughing it on tour was the norm. They undertake a jungle adventure, heading inland to connect with the indigenous Tae people.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are
programme.desc: Actor and writer Ruth Jones - Nessa from Gavin and Stacey - investigates her Welsh family’s history. On her mum’s side, she discovers that her great-great-great-grandfather was a mariner who rose to the rank of captain in the domestic coastal trade. His son surpassed his father by carrying Welsh coal across the world. On Ruth’s dad’s side, she looks into the career of the grandfather she never met. Henry Richard Jones was a leading light in the Medical Aid Societies of south Wales, which provided a model for the National Health Service in 1948. With their shopping bags full, the teams travel to nearby Hele in north Devon, where auctioneer Adam Partridge is on the rostrum selling them to the highest bidder.

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
When an exclusive, high-roller poker night ends with the murder of oil magnate and seemingly devoted family man Jeremy Hare, Rose and Raj find themselves completely out of their depth in the gambling world. The evidence is perplexing. Jeremy’s substantial winnings from the night are still on his body, and he’s been stabbed with an ornate, ceremonial golden knife that was left at the scene. Unfamiliar with the complex strategies and unspoken rules of high-stakes poker, Rose and Raj are left struggling to decipher the various hidden motives of the players around the table.
The game was hosted by Ace Dawso, a slick operator and local villain, with whom Joe and Rose have had a previous run-in. Ace’s invitation-only matches attract an elite, ruthless crowd. There’s Rami Ashraf, an enigmatic Egyptian playboy and seasoned poker pro with secrets to protect; Eleanor Calvert, a sharp stock-market whiz and one of the country’s wealthiest, most calculating women; and Ace himself, who sat out the fatal hand but oversaw the room with a watchful eye. Every player present had something to lose and possibly a reason to want Jeremy silenced.
Baffled by the tight-lipped suspects who can quickly tell that she doesn’t understand the game, Rose soon realises that conventional police work won't crack this case. She has no choice but to recruit Joe, whose history makes him the ultimate insider. Enticed back into the illicit world of gambling, Joe is forced to confront the dangerous addiction that nearly ruined his life. To help Rose read the table and flush out a cold-blooded killer, Joe must walk a risky tightrope, gambling not just with cash, but with his own addictions.

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
On All Saints’ Day, Pam Rhodes celebrates the life of St Francis of Assisi 800 years since his death and meets Christians still inspired by his teachings.
St Francis is one of the most well-known figures in Christian history. Famous for his profound love of nature, he is the patron saint of ecology and animals, and this year has been designated by Pope Leo XIV as a Franciscan jubilee year. Pam Rhodes explores how he has inspired others to follow in his footsteps and how his legacy of faith and care lives on.
In Liverpool, Pam meets Fr Maximilian Martin at St Anthony of Padua Friary to discover what it means to live as a Franciscan friar. He found his calling after ten years as a nurse, and he shares the timeless message of St Francis - simplicity, caring for creation and serving the vulnerable - while offering a glimpse into a life of poverty, chastity and obedience right in the heart of the local community.
In Salford, we visit the Laudato Si' Centre at Wardley Hall, the diocese's ambitious response to Pope Francis’s call to care for our common home. Environment and learning officer Emily Cahill leads a group of students from St Ambrose Barlow RC Secondary School on a retreat day. Getting their hands in the soil, the students discover the beauty of nature first-hand and learn how to become the next generation of guardians of creation.
Finally, Pam heads to Birkenhead to meet Steph Worsley, a dedicated veterinary nurse with nearly 27 years of experience. Raised in a Methodist farming community, Steph proudly wears the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons badge, which features St Francis at its centre as a daily reminder of her professional oath to respect and protect all animals.
1. For All the Saints - Chester Cathedral2. Make Me a Channel of Your Peace – St George’s RC Cathedral, Southwark 3. Way Maker - Gas Street Church, Birmingham4. Spirit and Truth - The Monastery, Manchester5. All Creatures of Our God and King - Our Lady's Church, York6. programme.title: Blue Planet II
programme.desc:
In recent years, our knowledge of life beneath the waves has been transformed. Using cutting-edge technology in this extended special, we celebrate the highlights from the series. From the intense heat of the tropics to our planet's frozen poles, through to its unexplored depths, we reveal new worlds and extraordinary, never-seen-before animal behaviours.
Starting in the tropical coral reefs - the most diverse ocean habitat - a tusk fish demonstrates a surprising level of ingenuity using corals as an anvil to break open clams. In the Seychelles, half a million terns nest on an island. Fledglings must eventually take to the wing, but danger lurks beneath the waves: metre-long giant trevally fish leap clear out of the water to snatch birds.
In the tropics, the sun heats the sea, creating rain, winds and huge storms that drive up towards higher latitudes. Here, the seas change with the seasons. In spring, thousands of mobula rays gather in Mexico's Sea of Cortez. At night, in a previously unseen event, tiny organisms that light up when disturbed react to their wingbeats, creating an enchanting bioluminescent firework display.
The seasonal seas are home to bountiful kelp forests. In the undersea forests of southern Africa, one resident - the common octopus - has become the ultimate escape artist. To outwit her nemesis, the pyjama shark, she uses ingenious tactics, never filmed before.
On the coast, two worlds collide. Where sea meets land, coasts are the most dynamic and challenging habitats in the ocean. The ever-changing tides create rock pools. But these temporary worlds are a battleground. Predatory starfish turn a magical garden into the stuff of nightmares.
The big blue is the world's greatest wilderness - a vast marine desert where there is little to eat and nowhere to hide. Sometimes, there is a brief explosion of food, but ocean hunters must be fast to make the best of this bonanza. We witness super-pods of up to 5,000 spinner dolphins racing to herd vast shoals of lanternfish, briefly caught at the surface where it is thought they spawn. New aerial footage reveals, for the first time, the spectacular feeding frenzy of 90kg tuna and dolphins smashing through the lantern fish shoals, turning the sea white with foam.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The warm, sunlit waters of the tropics support the greatest diversity of life in the ocean. Bathed in year-round sunlight for millions of years, these seas are home to more species than anywhere else on earth. In a world where competition is fierce, animals have evolved extraordinary ways to survive. Yet even in these seemingly familiar waters, remarkable new behaviours are still being discovered.
At the northern tip of Australia, a tawny nurse shark patrols the shallows in search of food. Too slow to chase fish in open water, it relies on a surprising strategy. Gathering in groups, the sharks appear to work together in a coordinated ambush. After waiting patiently in the shallows, they drive huge shoals of fish out of the water and onto the beach before vacuuming up their prey by the mouthful.
Further west, Shark Bay is home to one of the world's greatest concentrations of dolphins. Here, bottlenose dolphins have developed a hunting technique previously unknown to science. Carrying sea sponges to isolated coral bommies, they use them to block the hiding places of fish, creating one of the most sophisticated examples of trap-setting ever documented in the animal kingdom.
Across the tropics, coral reefs are bustling underwater cities where predators and prey are locked in a constant battle. In the Red Sea, coral groupers communicate with two very different hunting partners - giant Maori wrasse and sleek moray eels. Only by working together can they flush prey from the reef's maze of crevices, making the grouper far more successful than it could ever be alone. After dark in Bali, the reefs take a more sinister turn as harlequin shrimp stalk starfish for supper. Barely five centimetres long, these tiny hunters have developed a macabre way of overcoming prey many times their size.
Beyond the reefs lie immense plains of sand and mud. Here, humpback whales arrive after epic migrations from Antarctica. For one female, this will be her final journey. As she takes her last breath, hundreds of sharks gather nearby. In death, her body becomes a vital source of nutrients, feeding a host of scavengers and bringing life to one of the tropical seas' most barren landscapes.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc:
The story of Iranians who have lived through the most turbulent and traumatic of years, with widespread street protests, a brutal crackdown by the authorities and a war launched against Iran by the US and Israel.
The film follows one mother who begins the year planning a future with her daughter, only to see it end with a promise to avenge her daughter’s death. After she publicly blamed the Iranian authorities, she was forced to flee the country and live in exile.
A medic reveals how his life has changed after treating hundreds of protesters, many with gunshot wounds, while a man who also fled Iran in fear shares the last messages from a relative, sentenced to death.
Filmed both inside and outside the country, this is the raw and uncompromising story of a year in Iran, told by some of the people who were there. programme.title: Clickbait Clinic with Stacey Dooley
programme.sub-title: Can dog deworming tablets cure cancer ║ S1E6/6
programme.desc:
Stacey looks into an emotive and controversial trend claiming that over-the-counter dog deworming tablets fenbendazole can cure cancer. She meets Mel, a woman from Kent with stage four cancer, who decided to start the DIY treatment and chart her progress on her socials.
Further sleuthing takes Stacey to America to meet Joe Tippens, the originator of the trend, whose claims sparked nationwide panic buying of fenbendazole in South Korea. That leads Stacey to explore why medical trials have never been fully funded, and to ask Dr Alex and Dr Nighat about the potential side-effects and the benefits of sticking to NHS-approved treatments. programme.desc:

The pairs embark on a life-changing adventure - a 7,500km race from the prehistoric jungles of Borneo to the sun-baked southern tip of Australia.
Competing in this series are acclaimed singer-songwriter and musician Sam Ryder, and his best friend and tour manager, Kaz; veteran sports broadcaster Jeff Stelling and his son Matt; BRIT award-winning singer-songwriter Ella Eyre and childhood friend Nana; and influencer Princess Andre with her brother musician Junior Andre.
Stripped of their smartphones and bank cards, these household names will be tested; emotions will run high, and relationships will be transformed on an adventure that’s as challenging as it is rewarding. They will need to rely on their own resourcefulness and the kindness of strangers to reach the finish line, equipped with only a map and a budget of £26 each a day.
Their race begins in Kuching, a vibrant city in north west Malaysian Borneo and the gateway to the island's vast wilderness. From there, the teams must cross three countries and two continents, weaving through five checkpoints before reaching the finish line in Melbourne, Australia.
The teams must tackle the most formidable race yet - traversing the ancient jungles and indigenous heartlands of Borneo, navigating the Makassar Strait to Sulawesi, an island of cinematic, towering limestone cliffs, before reaching the kaleidoscopic splendour of Queensland's landscapes, from the turquoise blues of the Great Barrier Reef to the arid, expansive orange of the outback. Finally, they will thread through sprawling Sydney before reaching the finish line on the southern tip of Australia.
Musician Sam and tour manager Kaz embrace an unexpected start to the race and dive straight in, relishing the chance to revisit the early days of their friendship when roughing it on tour was the norm. They undertake a jungle adventure, heading inland to connect with the indigenous Tae people.

programme.desc: Actor and writer Ruth Jones - Nessa from Gavin and Stacey - investigates her Welsh family’s history. On her mum’s side, she discovers that her great-great-great-grandfather was a mariner who rose to the rank of captain in the domestic coastal trade. His son surpassed his father by carrying Welsh coal across the world. On Ruth’s dad’s side, she looks into the career of the grandfather she never met. Henry Richard Jones was a leading light in the Medical Aid Societies of south Wales, which provided a model for the National Health Service in 1948. programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
When an exclusive, high-roller poker night ends with the murder of oil magnate and seemingly devoted family man Jeremy Hare, Rose and Raj find themselves completely out of their depth in the gambling world. The evidence is perplexing. Jeremy’s substantial winnings from the night are still on his body, and he’s been stabbed with an ornate, ceremonial golden knife that was left at the scene. Unfamiliar with the complex strategies and unspoken rules of high-stakes poker, Rose and Raj are left struggling to decipher the various hidden motives of the players around the table.
The game was hosted by Ace Dawso, a slick operator and local villain, with whom Joe and Rose have had a previous run-in. Ace’s invitation-only matches attract an elite, ruthless crowd. There’s Rami Ashraf, an enigmatic Egyptian playboy and seasoned poker pro with secrets to protect; Eleanor Calvert, a sharp stock-market whiz and one of the country’s wealthiest, most calculating women; and Ace himself, who sat out the fatal hand but oversaw the room with a watchful eye. Every player present had something to lose and possibly a reason to want Jeremy silenced.
Baffled by the tight-lipped suspects who can quickly tell that she doesn’t understand the game, Rose soon realises that conventional police work won't crack this case. She has no choice but to recruit Joe, whose history makes him the ultimate insider. Enticed back into the illicit world of gambling, Joe is forced to confront the dangerous addiction that nearly ruined his life. To help Rose read the table and flush out a cold-blooded killer, Joe must walk a risky tightrope, gambling not just with cash, but with his own addictions.

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
On All Saints’ Day, Pam Rhodes celebrates the life of St Francis of Assisi 800 years since his death and meets Christians still inspired by his teachings.
St Francis is one of the most well-known figures in Christian history. Famous for his profound love of nature, he is the patron saint of ecology and animals, and this year has been designated by Pope Leo XIV as a Franciscan jubilee year. Pam Rhodes explores how he has inspired others to follow in his footsteps and how his legacy of faith and care lives on.
In Liverpool, Pam meets Fr Maximilian Martin at St Anthony of Padua Friary to discover what it means to live as a Franciscan friar. He found his calling after ten years as a nurse, and he shares the timeless message of St Francis - simplicity, caring for creation and serving the vulnerable - while offering a glimpse into a life of poverty, chastity and obedience right in the heart of the local community.
In Salford, we visit the Laudato Si' Centre at Wardley Hall, the diocese's ambitious response to Pope Francis’s call to care for our common home. Environment and learning officer Emily Cahill leads a group of students from St Ambrose Barlow RC Secondary School on a retreat day. Getting their hands in the soil, the students discover the beauty of nature first-hand and learn how to become the next generation of guardians of creation.
Finally, Pam heads to Birkenhead to meet Steph Worsley, a dedicated veterinary nurse with nearly 27 years of experience. Raised in a Methodist farming community, Steph proudly wears the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons badge, which features St Francis at its centre as a daily reminder of her professional oath to respect and protect all animals.
1. For All the Saints - Chester Cathedral2. Make Me a Channel of Your Peace – St George’s RC Cathedral, Southwark 3. Way Maker - Gas Street Church, Birmingham4. Spirit and Truth - The Monastery, Manchester5. All Creatures of Our God and King - Our Lady's Church, York6. programme.title: Blue Planet II
programme.desc:
In recent years, our knowledge of life beneath the waves has been transformed. Using cutting-edge technology in this extended special, we celebrate the highlights from the series. From the intense heat of the tropics to our planet's frozen poles, through to its unexplored depths, we reveal new worlds and extraordinary, never-seen-before animal behaviours.
Starting in the tropical coral reefs - the most diverse ocean habitat - a tusk fish demonstrates a surprising level of ingenuity using corals as an anvil to break open clams. In the Seychelles, half a million terns nest on an island. Fledglings must eventually take to the wing, but danger lurks beneath the waves: metre-long giant trevally fish leap clear out of the water to snatch birds.
In the tropics, the sun heats the sea, creating rain, winds and huge storms that drive up towards higher latitudes. Here, the seas change with the seasons. In spring, thousands of mobula rays gather in Mexico's Sea of Cortez. At night, in a previously unseen event, tiny organisms that light up when disturbed react to their wingbeats, creating an enchanting bioluminescent firework display.
The seasonal seas are home to bountiful kelp forests. In the undersea forests of southern Africa, one resident - the common octopus - has become the ultimate escape artist. To outwit her nemesis, the pyjama shark, she uses ingenious tactics, never filmed before.
On the coast, two worlds collide. Where sea meets land, coasts are the most dynamic and challenging habitats in the ocean. The ever-changing tides create rock pools. But these temporary worlds are a battleground. Predatory starfish turn a magical garden into the stuff of nightmares.
The big blue is the world's greatest wilderness - a vast marine desert where there is little to eat and nowhere to hide. Sometimes, there is a brief explosion of food, but ocean hunters must be fast to make the best of this bonanza. We witness super-pods of up to 5,000 spinner dolphins racing to herd vast shoals of lanternfish, briefly caught at the surface where it is thought they spawn. New aerial footage reveals, for the first time, the spectacular feeding frenzy of 90kg tuna and dolphins smashing through the lantern fish shoals, turning the sea white with foam.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The warm, sunlit waters of the tropics support the greatest diversity of life in the ocean. Bathed in year-round sunlight for millions of years, these seas are home to more species than anywhere else on earth. In a world where competition is fierce, animals have evolved extraordinary ways to survive. Yet even in these seemingly familiar waters, remarkable new behaviours are still being discovered.
At the northern tip of Australia, a tawny nurse shark patrols the shallows in search of food. Too slow to chase fish in open water, it relies on a surprising strategy. Gathering in groups, the sharks appear to work together in a coordinated ambush. After waiting patiently in the shallows, they drive huge shoals of fish out of the water and onto the beach before vacuuming up their prey by the mouthful.
Further west, Shark Bay is home to one of the world's greatest concentrations of dolphins. Here, bottlenose dolphins have developed a hunting technique previously unknown to science. Carrying sea sponges to isolated coral bommies, they use them to block the hiding places of fish, creating one of the most sophisticated examples of trap-setting ever documented in the animal kingdom.
Across the tropics, coral reefs are bustling underwater cities where predators and prey are locked in a constant battle. In the Red Sea, coral groupers communicate with two very different hunting partners - giant Maori wrasse and sleek moray eels. Only by working together can they flush prey from the reef's maze of crevices, making the grouper far more successful than it could ever be alone. After dark in Bali, the reefs take a more sinister turn as harlequin shrimp stalk starfish for supper. Barely five centimetres long, these tiny hunters have developed a macabre way of overcoming prey many times their size.
Beyond the reefs lie immense plains of sand and mud. Here, humpback whales arrive after epic migrations from Antarctica. For one female, this will be her final journey. As she takes her last breath, hundreds of sharks gather nearby. In death, her body becomes a vital source of nutrients, feeding a host of scavengers and bringing life to one of the tropical seas' most barren landscapes.

The story of Iranians who have lived through the most turbulent and traumatic of years, with widespread street protests, a brutal crackdown by the authorities and a war launched against Iran by the US and Israel.

programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc:
Four familiar faces paired with a friend or a loved one leave their luxury lifestyles at the starting line for a journey that will take them to the other side of the world and push them to the limits of their endurance. The pairs embark on a life-changing adventure - a 7,500km race from the prehistoric jungles of Borneo to the sun-baked southern tip of Australia.
Competing in this series are acclaimed singer-songwriter and musician Sam Ryder, and his best friend and tour manager, Kaz; veteran sports broadcaster Jeff Stelling and his son Matt; BRIT award-winning singer-songwriter Ella Eyre and childhood friend Nana; and influencer Princess Andre with her brother musician Junior Andre.
Stripped of their smartphones and bank cards, these household names will be tested; emotions will run high, and relationships will be transformed on an adventure that’s as challenging as it is rewarding. They will need to rely on their own resourcefulness and the kindness of strangers to reach the finish line, equipped with only a map and a budget of £26 each a day.
Their race begins in Kuching, a vibrant city in north west Malaysian Borneo and the gateway to the island's vast wilderness. From there, the teams must cross three countries and two continents, weaving through five checkpoints before reaching the finish line in Melbourne, Australia.
The teams must tackle the most formidable race yet - traversing the ancient jungles and indigenous heartlands of Borneo, navigating the Makassar Strait to Sulawesi, an island of cinematic, towering limestone cliffs, before reaching the kaleidoscopic splendour of Queensland's landscapes, from the turquoise blues of the Great Barrier Reef to the arid, expansive orange of the outback. Finally, they will thread through sprawling Sydney before reaching the finish line on the southern tip of Australia.
Musician Sam and tour manager Kaz embrace an unexpected start to the race and dive straight in, relishing the chance to revisit the early days of their friendship when roughing it on tour was the norm. They undertake a jungle adventure, heading inland to connect with the indigenous Tae people.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are
programme.desc: Actor and writer Ruth Jones - Nessa from Gavin and Stacey - investigates her Welsh family’s history. On her mum’s side, she discovers that her great-great-great-grandfather was a mariner who rose to the rank of captain in the domestic coastal trade. His son surpassed his father by carrying Welsh coal across the world. On Ruth’s dad’s side, she looks into the career of the grandfather she never met. Henry Richard Jones was a leading light in the Medical Aid Societies of south Wales, which provided a model for the National Health Service in 1948. programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
When an exclusive, high-roller poker night ends with the murder of oil magnate and seemingly devoted family man Jeremy Hare, Rose and Raj find themselves completely out of their depth in the gambling world. The evidence is perplexing. Jeremy’s substantial winnings from the night are still on his body, and he’s been stabbed with an ornate, ceremonial golden knife that was left at the scene. Unfamiliar with the complex strategies and unspoken rules of high-stakes poker, Rose and Raj are left struggling to decipher the various hidden motives of the players around the table.
The game was hosted by Ace Dawso, a slick operator and local villain, with whom Joe and Rose have had a previous run-in. Ace’s invitation-only matches attract an elite, ruthless crowd. There’s Rami Ashraf, an enigmatic Egyptian playboy and seasoned poker pro with secrets to protect; Eleanor Calvert, a sharp stock-market whiz and one of the country’s wealthiest, most calculating women; and Ace himself, who sat out the fatal hand but oversaw the room with a watchful eye. Every player present had something to lose and possibly a reason to want Jeremy silenced.
Baffled by the tight-lipped suspects who can quickly tell that she doesn’t understand the game, Rose soon realises that conventional police work won't crack this case. She has no choice but to recruit Joe, whose history makes him the ultimate insider. Enticed back into the illicit world of gambling, Joe is forced to confront the dangerous addiction that nearly ruined his life. To help Rose read the table and flush out a cold-blooded killer, Joe must walk a risky tightrope, gambling not just with cash, but with his own addictions.

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
On All Saints’ Day, Pam Rhodes celebrates the life of St Francis of Assisi 800 years since his death and meets Christians still inspired by his teachings.
St Francis is one of the most well-known figures in Christian history. Famous for his profound love of nature, he is the patron saint of ecology and animals, and this year has been designated by Pope Leo XIV as a Franciscan jubilee year. Pam Rhodes explores how he has inspired others to follow in his footsteps and how his legacy of faith and care lives on.
In Liverpool, Pam meets Fr Maximilian Martin at St Anthony of Padua Friary to discover what it means to live as a Franciscan friar. He found his calling after ten years as a nurse, and he shares the timeless message of St Francis - simplicity, caring for creation and serving the vulnerable - while offering a glimpse into a life of poverty, chastity and obedience right in the heart of the local community.
In Salford, we visit the Laudato Si' Centre at Wardley Hall, the diocese's ambitious response to Pope Francis’s call to care for our common home. Environment and learning officer Emily Cahill leads a group of students from St Ambrose Barlow RC Secondary School on a retreat day. Getting their hands in the soil, the students discover the beauty of nature first-hand and learn how to become the next generation of guardians of creation.
Finally, Pam heads to Birkenhead to meet Steph Worsley, a dedicated veterinary nurse with nearly 27 years of experience. Raised in a Methodist farming community, Steph proudly wears the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons badge, which features St Francis at its centre as a daily reminder of her professional oath to respect and protect all animals.

programme.title: Blue Planet II
programme.desc:
In recent years, our knowledge of life beneath the waves has been transformed. Using cutting-edge technology in this extended special, we celebrate the highlights from the series. From the intense heat of the tropics to our planet's frozen poles, through to its unexplored depths, we reveal new worlds and extraordinary, never-seen-before animal behaviours.
Starting in the tropical coral reefs - the most diverse ocean habitat - a tusk fish demonstrates a surprising level of ingenuity using corals as an anvil to break open clams. In the Seychelles, half a million terns nest on an island. Fledglings must eventually take to the wing, but danger lurks beneath the waves: metre-long giant trevally fish leap clear out of the water to snatch birds.
In the tropics, the sun heats the sea, creating rain, winds and huge storms that drive up towards higher latitudes. Here, the seas change with the seasons. In spring, thousands of mobula rays gather in Mexico's Sea of Cortez. At night, in a previously unseen event, tiny organisms that light up when disturbed react to their wingbeats, creating an enchanting bioluminescent firework display.
The seasonal seas are home to bountiful kelp forests. In the undersea forests of southern Africa, one resident - the common octopus - has become the ultimate escape artist. To outwit her nemesis, the pyjama shark, she uses ingenious tactics, never filmed before.
On the coast, two worlds collide. Where sea meets land, coasts are the most dynamic and challenging habitats in the ocean. The ever-changing tides create rock pools. But these temporary worlds are a battleground. Predatory starfish turn a magical garden into the stuff of nightmares.
The big blue is the world's greatest wilderness - a vast marine desert where there is little to eat and nowhere to hide. Sometimes, there is a brief explosion of food, but ocean hunters must be fast to make the best of this bonanza. We witness super-pods of up to 5,000 spinner dolphins racing to herd vast shoals of lanternfish, briefly caught at the surface where it is thought they spawn. New aerial footage reveals, for the first time, the spectacular feeding frenzy of 90kg tuna and dolphins smashing through the lantern fish shoals, turning the sea white with foam.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The warm, sunlit waters of the tropics support the greatest diversity of life in the ocean. Bathed in year-round sunlight for millions of years, these seas are home to more species than anywhere else on earth. In a world where competition is fierce, animals have evolved extraordinary ways to survive. Yet even in these seemingly familiar waters, remarkable new behaviours are still being discovered.
At the northern tip of Australia, a tawny nurse shark patrols the shallows in search of food. Too slow to chase fish in open water, it relies on a surprising strategy. Gathering in groups, the sharks appear to work together in a coordinated ambush. After waiting patiently in the shallows, they drive huge shoals of fish out of the water and onto the beach before vacuuming up their prey by the mouthful.
Further west, Shark Bay is home to one of the world's greatest concentrations of dolphins. Here, bottlenose dolphins have developed a hunting technique previously unknown to science. Carrying sea sponges to isolated coral bommies, they use them to block the hiding places of fish, creating one of the most sophisticated examples of trap-setting ever documented in the animal kingdom.
Across the tropics, coral reefs are bustling underwater cities where predators and prey are locked in a constant battle. In the Red Sea, coral groupers communicate with two very different hunting partners - giant Maori wrasse and sleek moray eels. Only by working together can they flush prey from the reef's maze of crevices, making the grouper far more successful than it could ever be alone. After dark in Bali, the reefs take a more sinister turn as harlequin shrimp stalk starfish for supper. Barely five centimetres long, these tiny hunters have developed a macabre way of overcoming prey many times their size.
Beyond the reefs lie immense plains of sand and mud. Here, humpback whales arrive after epic migrations from Antarctica. For one female, this will be her final journey. As she takes her last breath, hundreds of sharks gather nearby. In death, her body becomes a vital source of nutrients, feeding a host of scavengers and bringing life to one of the tropical seas' most barren landscapes.
