programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc:
Four familiar faces paired with a friend or a loved one leave their luxury lifestyles at the starting line for a journey that will take them to the other side of the world and push them to the limits of their endurance. The pairs embark on a life-changing adventure - a 7,500km race from the prehistoric jungles of Borneo to the sun-baked southern tip of Australia.
Competing in this series are acclaimed singer-songwriter and musician Sam Ryder, and his best friend and tour manager, Kaz; veteran sports broadcaster Jeff Stelling and his son Matt; BRIT award-winning singer-songwriter Ella Eyre and childhood friend Nana; and influencer Princess Andre with her brother musician Junior Andre.
Stripped of their smartphones and bank cards, these household names will be tested; emotions will run high, and relationships will be transformed on an adventure that’s as challenging as it is rewarding. They will need to rely on their own resourcefulness and the kindness of strangers to reach the finish line, equipped with only a map and a budget of £26 each a day.
Their race begins in Kuching, a vibrant city in north west Malaysian Borneo and the gateway to the island's vast wilderness. From there, the teams must cross three countries and two continents, weaving through five checkpoints before reaching the finish line in Melbourne, Australia.
The teams must tackle the most formidable race yet - traversing the ancient jungles and indigenous heartlands of Borneo, navigating the Makassar Strait to Sulawesi, an island of cinematic, towering limestone cliffs, before reaching the kaleidoscopic splendour of Queensland's landscapes, from the turquoise blues of the Great Barrier Reef to the arid, expansive orange of the outback. Finally, they will thread through sprawling Sydney before reaching the finish line on the southern tip of Australia.
Musician Sam and tour manager Kaz embrace an unexpected start to the race and dive straight in, relishing the chance to revisit the early days of their friendship when roughing it on tour was the norm. They undertake a jungle adventure, heading inland to connect with the indigenous Tae people.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are
programme.desc: Actor and writer Ruth Jones - Nessa from Gavin and Stacey - investigates her Welsh family’s history. On her mum’s side, she discovers that her great-great-great-grandfather was a mariner who rose to the rank of captain in the domestic coastal trade. His son surpassed his father by carrying Welsh coal across the world. On Ruth’s dad’s side, she looks into the career of the grandfather she never met. Henry Richard Jones was a leading light in the Medical Aid Societies of south Wales, which provided a model for the National Health Service in 1948. programme.title: The Celebrity Inner Circle
programme.desc:
Amanda Holden hosts this exciting quiz show, packed with strategy, high stakes and lots of surprises.
Five contestants choose a celebrity partner and are assigned a secret stash of cash, worth anything from zero to a whopping £6,000.
The twist? Each pair only knows their own value before being thrown into a battle of wits, nerve and strategic gameplay across a series of challenging rounds.
Their mission? Uncover who has got what amount, outsmart their rivals and secure their spot in the final. Each round brings tense showdowns, with the winning pair earning immunity and a game-changing power, before the group votes to cast a contestant and their celebrity partner out of the game.
Only two contestants will make it to the cash builder and the chance to double their combined cash before the dramatic final, where they must make the ultimate decision. Will they choose to split their combined prize money equally, or will one player attempt to take it all, leaving the other with nothing? In this show, it’s not just about what you know. It’s about who you can trust.

programme.desc:

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
When an exclusive, high-roller poker night ends with the murder of oil magnate and seemingly devoted family man Jeremy Hare, Rose and Raj find themselves completely out of their depth in the gambling world. The evidence is perplexing. Jeremy’s substantial winnings from the night are still on his body, and he’s been stabbed with an ornate, ceremonial golden knife that was left at the scene. Unfamiliar with the complex strategies and unspoken rules of high-stakes poker, Rose and Raj are left struggling to decipher the various hidden motives of the players around the table.
The game was hosted by Ace Dawso, a slick operator and local villain, with whom Joe and Rose have had a previous run-in. Ace’s invitation-only matches attract an elite, ruthless crowd. There’s Rami Ashraf, an enigmatic Egyptian playboy and seasoned poker pro with secrets to protect; Eleanor Calvert, a sharp stock-market whiz and one of the country’s wealthiest, most calculating women; and Ace himself, who sat out the fatal hand but oversaw the room with a watchful eye. Every player present had something to lose and possibly a reason to want Jeremy silenced.
Baffled by the tight-lipped suspects who can quickly tell that she doesn’t understand the game, Rose soon realises that conventional police work won't crack this case. She has no choice but to recruit Joe, whose history makes him the ultimate insider. Enticed back into the illicit world of gambling, Joe is forced to confront the dangerous addiction that nearly ruined his life. To help Rose read the table and flush out a cold-blooded killer, Joe must walk a risky tightrope, gambling not just with cash, but with his own addictions.

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
On All Saints’ Day, Pam Rhodes celebrates the life of St Francis of Assisi 800 years since his death and meets Christians still inspired by his teachings.
St Francis is one of the most well-known figures in Christian history. Famous for his profound love of nature, he is the patron saint of ecology and animals, and this year has been designated by Pope Leo XIV as a Franciscan jubilee year. Pam Rhodes explores how he has inspired others to follow in his footsteps and how his legacy of faith and care lives on.
In Liverpool, Pam meets Fr Maximilian Martin at St Anthony of Padua Friary to discover what it means to live as a Franciscan friar. He found his calling after ten years as a nurse, and he shares the timeless message of St Francis - simplicity, caring for creation and serving the vulnerable - while offering a glimpse into a life of poverty, chastity and obedience right in the heart of the local community.
In Salford, we visit the Laudato Si' Centre at Wardley Hall, the diocese's ambitious response to Pope Francis’s call to care for our common home. Environment and learning officer Emily Cahill leads a group of students from St Ambrose Barlow RC Secondary School on a retreat day. Getting their hands in the soil, the students discover the beauty of nature first-hand and learn how to become the next generation of guardians of creation.
Finally, Pam heads to Birkenhead to meet Steph Worsley, a dedicated veterinary nurse with nearly 27 years of experience. Raised in a Methodist farming community, Steph proudly wears the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons badge, which features St Francis at its centre as a daily reminder of her professional oath to respect and protect all animals.
1. For All the Saints - Chester Cathedral2. Make Me a Channel of Your Peace – St George’s RC Cathedral, Southwark 3. Way Maker - Gas Street Church, Birmingham4. Spirit and Truth - The Monastery, Manchester5. All Creatures of Our God and King - Our Lady's Church, York6. programme.title: Blue Planet II
programme.desc:
In recent years, our knowledge of life beneath the waves has been transformed. Using cutting-edge technology in this extended special, we celebrate the highlights from the series. From the intense heat of the tropics to our planet's frozen poles, through to its unexplored depths, we reveal new worlds and extraordinary, never-seen-before animal behaviours.
Starting in the tropical coral reefs - the most diverse ocean habitat - a tusk fish demonstrates a surprising level of ingenuity using corals as an anvil to break open clams. In the Seychelles, half a million terns nest on an island. Fledglings must eventually take to the wing, but danger lurks beneath the waves: metre-long giant trevally fish leap clear out of the water to snatch birds.
In the tropics, the sun heats the sea, creating rain, winds and huge storms that drive up towards higher latitudes. Here, the seas change with the seasons. In spring, thousands of mobula rays gather in Mexico's Sea of Cortez. At night, in a previously unseen event, tiny organisms that light up when disturbed react to their wingbeats, creating an enchanting bioluminescent firework display.
The seasonal seas are home to bountiful kelp forests. In the undersea forests of southern Africa, one resident - the common octopus - has become the ultimate escape artist. To outwit her nemesis, the pyjama shark, she uses ingenious tactics, never filmed before.
On the coast, two worlds collide. Where sea meets land, coasts are the most dynamic and challenging habitats in the ocean. The ever-changing tides create rock pools. But these temporary worlds are a battleground. Predatory starfish turn a magical garden into the stuff of nightmares.
The big blue is the world's greatest wilderness - a vast marine desert where there is little to eat and nowhere to hide. Sometimes, there is a brief explosion of food, but ocean hunters must be fast to make the best of this bonanza. We witness super-pods of up to 5,000 spinner dolphins racing to herd vast shoals of lanternfish, briefly caught at the surface where it is thought they spawn. New aerial footage reveals, for the first time, the spectacular feeding frenzy of 90kg tuna and dolphins smashing through the lantern fish shoals, turning the sea white with foam.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The warm, sunlit waters of the tropics support the greatest diversity of life in the ocean. Bathed in year-round sunlight for millions of years, these seas are home to more species than anywhere else on earth. In a world where competition is fierce, animals have evolved extraordinary ways to survive. Yet even in these seemingly familiar waters, remarkable new behaviours are still being discovered.
At the northern tip of Australia, a tawny nurse shark patrols the shallows in search of food. Too slow to chase fish in open water, it relies on a surprising strategy. Gathering in groups, the sharks appear to work together in a coordinated ambush. After waiting patiently in the shallows, they drive huge shoals of fish out of the water and onto the beach before vacuuming up their prey by the mouthful.
Further west, Shark Bay is home to one of the world's greatest concentrations of dolphins. Here, bottlenose dolphins have developed a hunting technique previously unknown to science. Carrying sea sponges to isolated coral bommies, they use them to block the hiding places of fish, creating one of the most sophisticated examples of trap-setting ever documented in the animal kingdom.
Across the tropics, coral reefs are bustling underwater cities where predators and prey are locked in a constant battle. In the Red Sea, coral groupers communicate with two very different hunting partners - giant Maori wrasse and sleek moray eels. Only by working together can they flush prey from the reef's maze of crevices, making the grouper far more successful than it could ever be alone. After dark in Bali, the reefs take a more sinister turn as harlequin shrimp stalk starfish for supper. Barely five centimetres long, these tiny hunters have developed a macabre way of overcoming prey many times their size.
Beyond the reefs lie immense plains of sand and mud. Here, humpback whales arrive after epic migrations from Antarctica. For one female, this will be her final journey. As she takes her last breath, hundreds of sharks gather nearby. In death, her body becomes a vital source of nutrients, feeding a host of scavengers and bringing life to one of the tropical seas' most barren landscapes.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: Romford to the Blackwater Estuary ║ S16E17/20
programme.desc:

He arrives on the London Overground’s Liberty Line to visit a state-of-the-art rail-operating centre responsible for the whole of the East Anglian rail network. He discovers how signallers and operators control the movements of over 4,000 trains a day and learns how they respond to emergencies on the tracks.
At Upminster, he finds the gateway to the Chafford Gorges Nature Park, which for centuries was exploited for its natural resources. The former chalk quarries have been transformed into a rare habitat for orchids, and he hears how archaeologists have discovered Neanderthal stone tools in the chalky cliffs.
Michael takes a scenic rail journey through the marshy landscape of the Dengie Peninsula to arrive at a marina on the River Blackwater. programme.title: Earth’s Tropical Islands
programme.desc:
In the heart of south east Asia lies the tropical island of Borneo. Twice the size of the British Isles, it is the third largest island on earth and home to possibly the greatest diversity of life of any island - from flying lizards sun bears to orangutans. Its huge variety of habitats, from bustling coral reefs and ancient jungles to towering mountains, has given rise to over 60,000 species of plants and animals - many found nowhere else on earth.
Borneo’s shoreline is fringed by a tangle of mangroves and flooded forests, home to an extraordinary creature – the proboscis monkey. Their unique pot bellies allow them to survive on the nutrient-poor leaves, but even so, they must continually search for the freshest shoots. This means the whole family must cross one of many rivers that cut through the forest – patrolled by giant crocodiles. It is a drama rarely seen.
The island of Borneo is surrounded by some of the richest coral reefs in the world – a single reef can support more species of coral than the entire Caribbean Sea! This remarkable abundance attracted seafaring nomads, the Bajau Laut, ‘people of the sea’. Over generations their bodies have transformed, making them the ultimate human divers – but they are having to adapt to the modern world – using ingenuity to turn plastic waste that washes up on the beach to their advantage.
Heading inland are ancient forests, home to giants – the dipterocarps. Towering up to 100 metres high, they are the tallest rainforest trees in the world. A single tree can hold a thousand different species, and this intense competition has driven many animals to evolve in wondrous ways – on this island reptiles can fly.
At night, this competition in the jungle intensifies as many of Borneo’s 180 species of frog call for a mate. The bigger the frog, the louder the call: a problem for one of the smallest frogs on the island. In this never-before-filmed sequence, a male tree-hole frog, barely larger than a thumbnail, has come up with an ingenious solution to being heard above the noise.
Compared to the abundance of life in the treetops, the forest floor is an impoverished world. With little to eat, many of Borneo’s terrestrial mammals are smaller than on the mainland – including the exceedingly rare Bornean sun bear.

programme.title: Surgeons: At the Edge of Life
programme.desc:
Addenbrooke’s Hospital in Cambridge takes on some of the most challenging medical cases in the country. Its surgeons carry out operations that require such expertise that they are only performed here and in a handful of other UK centres.
One such procedure is a pelvic exenteration, so complicated it requires two surgeons to perform and two days to complete. The surgeons - colorectal consultant Nicola Fearnhead and consultant urologist Alex Colquhoun - only do around ten of these operations each year, where due to widespread cancer, all the organs in the pelvis need to be removed. It is such a massive, life-changing surgery that about 50 per cent of people who need the procedure for otherwise terminal illness, decide not to have it.
This time, their patient is 52-year-old Stuart, a father of two who has already had treatment for bowel cancer. However, the cancer has returned and the pelvic exenteration is his only chance for a cure. It will involve removing his rectum, bladder, prostate, surrounding lymph nodes as well as a large tumour on his kidney. The surgery is so radical it will leave him with no sexual function and needing two stomas; one for waste from his bowel and the other for urine.
On the first day of surgery, Nicola and Alex concentrate on taking out the disease. They must operate deep within Stuart’s pelvis to separate out the cancer and affected organs from the surrounding tissue and blood vessels. It is high-risk surgery because they need to operate near the body’s biggest blood vessels - the aorta and inferior vena cava - and the major vessels that branch off them. Damaging any of these could cause a major bleed.
But even if they manage to clear the disease, they still need a second day to reconstruct and create the two stomas. The most difficult one to create is for the urine produced by Stuart’s kidneys. Because his bladder will be removed, the drainage tubes from the kidneys – called ureters – need to be rerouted. This involves attaching these fragile tubes to a section of harvested bowel that will act as an outlet tube, which then has to be threaded through the abdominal wall to the surface without any kinks or distortions.

programme.title: Earth’s Tropical Islands
programme.desc:
This is a journey across Hawaii’s varied islands, discovering how they were made and the incredible wildlife that thrives there.
Hawaii is the most remote island chain on earth, and its tropical shores are hard to reach. But for the hardy creatures that can make it here, like the waterfall-climbing fish, carnivorous caterpillar and Laysan albatross, a land of opportunity awaits. From newly formed lava fields to lush jungles and vibrant coral reefs, these diverse and beautiful islands have it all.
Packed with surprising stories, the hidden gems of this tropical paradise are uncovered using stunning photography. Dramatic footage of the humpback whale heat run – the biggest courtship battle in the world – and intimate views of the world’s oldest known bird feeding its chick are just some of the highlights of what Hawaii has to offer.
The islands are so isolated that it used to be that one new species arrived every 100,000 years, but the arrival of people has radically changed the face of Hawaii. Now it gains around 20 new species every year. The remarkable Jackson’s chameleon is one of the animals recently introduced. Showing off its voracious appetite, the programme reveals how it is eating its way through the native animals and contributing to wiping them out entirely.
But this is a place where people are looking to the future and attempting to bring wildlife back from the brink of extinction. White terns, once extinct on the main islands of Hawaii, have gone from a single pair to over 2,000 birds in the last 60 years. It is a huge challenge, but people are seeking progressive new ways to live alongside nature to allow Hawaii’s wildlife to continue to thrive. Narrator - David Harewood Series Producer - Kathryn Jeffs Executive Producer - Mark Brownlow Production Manager - Dulcie Arnold Producer - Evie Wright Composer - Michael Kruk.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
First into the barn is Alistair Waite, with a fragile cake topper from his parents’ wedding cake, which holds memories of a childhood spent growing up in the circus. The centrepiece of the miniature circus scene is a faithful reproduction of the big top, of which Alistair’s father was the tent manager and where his mother performed each night. Paper restorer Angelina Bakalarou takes on the delicate task of restoring this precious memento, preserving a unique piece of circus heritage and family love.
Next in comes former children’s TV presenter Jenny Hanley, who brings along a cherished toy of great historical and personal significance: a stuffed monkey named Alphonse. This cheeky primate helped Jenny’s grandmother, Lisa Sheridan, take a series of relaxed and intimate portraits of the royal family, most notably of the young Princesses Elizabeth and Margaret. It was Alphonse’s job to attract the subject’s attention to the camera, but now, threadbare and worn, he’s in no condition to turn heads, royal or otherwise. It’s down to Bear Ladies Julie and Amanda to weave their magic, and bring him back to peak condition.
Londoner Abdul and his daughter Hannah are next through the barn doors, with a challenging proposal for horologist Steve Fletcher and woodworker Will Kirk. Their beautiful but very broken regulator clock was the dearest possession of Abdul’s father, who had been gifted it by a much-loved friend. Passed down to Abdul on his father’s death, the clock sadly didn’t survive the passage from India, and it is now in a pitiful state, leaving Abdul racked with guilt. It takes all of Will and Steve’s skills – and the help of a new face in the barn, screen printer Alasdair MacKay – to get this precious heirloom back to its very best.
Finally, Maureen Armstrong from Bristol presents a battered helmet from the Second World War era for the close attention of Lucia Scalisi. The helmet belonged to Maureen’s much-missed grandmother Dot, who served as a volunteer nurse during the Blitz and wore the helmet on duty as she tended to the wounded during bombing raids on Portsmouth. Now flaking and rust-spattered, Lucia sets to work to ensure that its history – and Dot’s name – are preserved for future generations.

programme.title: Escaping Idi Amin
programme.desc:
In August 1972, Idi Amin is 18 months into his dictatorship. Supporters hail the new president - a former boxer and soldier - as a saviour, and his rise to power is greeted with celebration and hope across Uganda.
But beneath the apparent social harmony, resentment runs deep. Until 1962, Uganda had been a protectorate of the British - with the British very much at the top of the pile, Africans at the bottom and Asians in the middle. Despite ten years of independence, many Africans feel that they are denied opportunities to improve their position in society. Idi Amin decides to exploit their feelings and increase support for his regime.
With one announcement from the president, the lives of 80,000 people in Uganda are changed forever. In a bid to cement his leadership, Idi Amin announces that all Ugandan Asians must leave the country within 90 days. Will they be able to flee on their British passports? programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc:
Michael Portillo’s exploration of Essex reaches Chelmsford. At a huge construction site on the outskirts of the city he discovers Beaulieu Park, the first railway station to be built on the Great Eastern Main Line for over 100 years. Michael learns how the station is designed to alleviate congestion in Chelmsford city centre.

Michael continues his rail journey on the Great Eastern Main Line and visits the historic riverside town of Maldon, with its pretty Thames barges. Michael learns about a medieval battle and handles a rare Viking sword.
He finishes this leg of his Essex journey in the coastal village of Tollesbury, with its strong maritime heritage and marshy landscape, a haven for birds and wildlife. programme.desc:
With the assistance of her daughter Maryam, Nadiya shares go-to family bakes that are as foolproof and fuss-free as they are delicious.
First up, Nadiya and Maryam, a self-confessed ‘flapjack fanatic’, share their ultimate recipe for this classic family favourite. The quick and effortless recipe features sweet, sticky oats sandwiching a secret layer of sharp raspberry jam and smothered in a triple chocolate topping.
Next, Nadiya turns the simple sandwich into a family feast with her triple-stack tandoori naan sandwich. It features succulent tandoori chicken breast wedged between three layers of soft naan and smothered in minty mayo, crisp apple cabbage and crunchy poppadoms.
Then, Nadiya’s spicing up a boring mid-week meal with her punchy Mexican one-pot wonder. This twist on chilli nachos, with gently spiced minced beef loaded with crunchy tortilla strips, rich oozy cheese, and topped with fresh jalapenos, is designed to put the fun back into family meals in one easy bake.
Last up is an epic chocolate cookie pie, with a deep filling of chocolate hazelnut spread and crispy wafers encased in a chewy chocolate chip cookie dough pie crust. With minimal effort, this extraordinary bake caters for 16 people.
Meanwhile, baker Louise Nicholson shares her colourful vegan bakes, such as her signature Highland cow and unicorn cupcake, that have taken Edinburgh by storm. programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc:
Four familiar faces paired with a friend or a loved one leave their luxury lifestyles at the starting line for a journey that will take them to the other side of the world and push them to the limits of their endurance. The pairs embark on a life-changing adventure - a 7,500km race from the prehistoric jungles of Borneo to the sun-baked southern tip of Australia.
Competing in this series are acclaimed singer-songwriter and musician Sam Ryder, and his best friend and tour manager, Kaz; veteran sports broadcaster Jeff Stelling and his son Matt; BRIT award-winning singer-songwriter Ella Eyre and childhood friend Nana; and influencer Princess Andre with her brother musician Junior Andre.
Stripped of their smartphones and bank cards, these household names will be tested; emotions will run high, and relationships will be transformed on an adventure that’s as challenging as it is rewarding. They will need to rely on their own resourcefulness and the kindness of strangers to reach the finish line, equipped with only a map and a budget of £26 each a day.
Their race begins in Kuching, a vibrant city in north west Malaysian Borneo and the gateway to the island's vast wilderness. From there, the teams must cross three countries and two continents, weaving through five checkpoints before reaching the finish line in Melbourne, Australia.
The teams must tackle the most formidable race yet - traversing the ancient jungles and indigenous heartlands of Borneo, navigating the Makassar Strait to Sulawesi, an island of cinematic, towering limestone cliffs, before reaching the kaleidoscopic splendour of Queensland's landscapes, from the turquoise blues of the Great Barrier Reef to the arid, expansive orange of the outback. Finally, they will thread through sprawling Sydney before reaching the finish line on the southern tip of Australia.
Musician Sam and tour manager Kaz embrace an unexpected start to the race and dive straight in, relishing the chance to revisit the early days of their friendship when roughing it on tour was the norm. They undertake a jungle adventure, heading inland to connect with the indigenous Tae people.

programme.title: True North
programme.desc:
In Derry-Londonderry, a once deeply divided city comes together to share a collective fascination with ghosts, ghouls and the stuff of nightmares.
In 1985, at the height of The Troubles, a Halloween-themed fancy-dress party in a local pub did something remarkable: it united a divided community. Forty years later, the small party that started as a fun distraction has grown into Europe’s largest Halloween festival, leaving the entire city spellbound.
We follow the ordinary people behind the extraordinary spectacle as they create and build the street theatre, costumes and art that bring Derry Halloween to life.
But this year isn’t without its own mischief and mayhem, from gale-force winds and structural collapses to wrangling a 50-metre snake.
Bringing together schools, youth clubs, dance troupes, workshops, costume makers and drumming bands, this is the story of a diverse city, young and old, dancing together in the streets, bound by a shared tradition, a fierce community spirit and an obsession with the dark arts of Halloween!

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc:
Derek is island-hopping in this round-up of his favourite Welsh island walks.
He goes wild in west Wales as he sails to Skomer Island – a national nature reserve of international importance due to its seabirds - where he gets a close-up view of the puffins, razorbills and guillemots before staying up late to see the Manx shearwater.
Next, Derek goes to Flat Holm Island, where he braves a huge colony of seagulls and discovers more about the island's past, including some Victorian gun placements.
Lastly, Derek heads up north to Wales's largest island, Anglesey, where he visits another tiny island with a secluded chapel, an unexpected motor racing track, a neolithic burial chamber and a sauna on a beach. Presenter - Derek Brockway Director - Leanne Rene Production Manager - Moira Edwards Executive Producer - Paul Tucker.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc:
Matt Tebbutt dishes up a feast of food from the Saturday Kitchen archives to whet the appetite for the week ahead.
The Hairy Bikers bring comfort food bang up to date with sticky Szechuan lamb, stuffed into pillowy soft bao buns, with a fresh hit of pickled carrots, spring onion and herbs – cosy comfort with a fragrant Asian twist! Meera Sodha introduces a taste of Sri Lanka to the studio as she continues the comfort theme with her warming lentil and coconut dal with crispy mustard kale.
Jeremy Lee brings his effervescent charm and wit to the kitchen whilst giving an underused cut of meat its chance in the spotlight. He makes a rich steamed kid pudding that melts in the mouth.
Mary McCartney celebrates Bonfire Night with her flavour-packed smoky dogs, before Carmen O’Neal and Idris Elba team up to serve a masterclass in brandy. And queen of puddings Nigella Lawson tucks into either her food heaven, scallops, or her food hell, candied fruit.
Meanwhile, Rick Stein explores the New Forest's bounty of produce, and the Hairy Bikers make a Menorcan dish in the Mediterranean Sea. programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc:
Sitting between Germany and France, Alsace is frontier land with a cuisine to match. In Strasbourg, Eva stops off at Brasserie Le Tigre for a beer (brassier means ‘to brew’) and a deliciously creamy tarte flambee. Then there's a trip to guide Coralie Andt’s restaurant, known as a winstub, where French wines can be enjoyed with plenty of cheese and sausage – as well as more sausage with sauerkraut cooked in white Riesling wine.
With French tarts in a brasserie that serves German-style beer, and German sausage in a winstub serving French white wine, Alsace is defined by its competing national influences.

programme.title: Wild Horses, the Rockies and Me
programme.desc:
As summer comes to a close, wildlife film-maker Gordon Buchanan ventures deep into the epic majesty of Canada’s Rocky Mountains in search of one of nature’s most iconic animals: wild horses. Powerful, dangerous and elusive, wild horses are icons of the untamed west, yet they are surprisingly overlooked by science, and their lives remain largely undocumented. As a keen rider in his youth, Gordon aims to change that.
Set against the stunning peaks, open grasslands and shadowy pine forests that fringe the eastern slopes of the Rockies, Gordon rides out on his own steed hoping to get to places only a wild horse can reach. After a series of setbacks, he eventually finds a family of so-called wildies that consists of two competing stallions, two mares and their two young foals, and starts bearing witness to their behaviour. Which of the two stallions, Red or Crusoe, is the father of the foals, and who will earn the right to lead the band? What motivates Red to keep the band separated away from the super-herd that gathers each day? Would it not be wiser to join up with other horses to guard against ravenous grizzly bears and wolves looking to fatten up for winter? Will the innocence and curiosity of the two foals, Socks and Boots, get them into trouble?
To understand more about the horses, and in particular this unusual family, Gordon immerses himself further into their world, attempting to befriend them and hoping to earn their trust as he seeks to experience their lives from within a herd of wild horses, something that hasn’t been attempted before.
Gordon must move carefully and think like a wild horse. However, this is not without its dangers, as one well-placed kick could be fatal, meaning he must learn to read the subtle language of flicking ears, stamping hooves and quiet glances that reveal what the horses are telling each other about him, uncovering their complex intelligence and close family bonds.
As he begins to gain acceptance into the herd, Gordon discovers that they face a greater danger than wild predators: the threat of being culled. He realises the devastating impact this would have on family groups, as well as on the fragile ecosystems they help to shape.

programme.title: BBC Young Musician
programme.desc:
From hundreds of entries, just three talented, young classical musicians remain as BBC Young Musician reaches its thrilling finale. This competition has launched the careers of some of the biggest stars in classical music, including Nicola Benedetti, Alison Balsom and Sheku Kanneh-Mason. At the end of the evening, another exceptional musician will be crowned to follow in their footsteps.
The final is the ultimate test for the three remaining players as they perform a full concerto with a professional orchestra in front of a packed auditorium at Bristol Beacon. We follow their progress during rehearsals and find out exactly what it takes to perform at this level.
Accompanying our finalists is the BBC National Orchestra of Wales, with internationally renowned conductor Alpesh Chauhan. Petroc Trelawny brings us exclusive backstage access and full performances from the evening. Returning to the jury are our series judges, critically acclaimed pianist Joanna MacGregor and award-winning conductor Ben Gernon.
For the exciting finale, they are joined on the judging panel by celebrated composer and current Master of the King’s Music, Errollyn Wallen. Only they can decide who will be named BBC Young Musician 2026. programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The warm, sunlit waters of the tropics support the greatest diversity of life in the ocean. Bathed in year-round sunlight for millions of years, these seas are home to more species than anywhere else on earth. In a world where competition is fierce, animals have evolved extraordinary ways to survive. Yet even in these seemingly familiar waters, remarkable new behaviours are still being discovered.
At the northern tip of Australia, a tawny nurse shark patrols the shallows in search of food. Too slow to chase fish in open water, it relies on a surprising strategy. Gathering in groups, the sharks appear to work together in a coordinated ambush. After waiting patiently in the shallows, they drive huge shoals of fish out of the water and onto the beach before vacuuming up their prey by the mouthful.
Further west, Shark Bay is home to one of the world's greatest concentrations of dolphins. Here, bottlenose dolphins have developed a hunting technique previously unknown to science. Carrying sea sponges to isolated coral bommies, they use them to block the hiding places of fish, creating one of the most sophisticated examples of trap-setting ever documented in the animal kingdom.
Across the tropics, coral reefs are bustling underwater cities where predators and prey are locked in a constant battle. In the Red Sea, coral groupers communicate with two very different hunting partners - giant Maori wrasse and sleek moray eels. Only by working together can they flush prey from the reef's maze of crevices, making the grouper far more successful than it could ever be alone. After dark in Bali, the reefs take a more sinister turn as harlequin shrimp stalk starfish for supper. Barely five centimetres long, these tiny hunters have developed a macabre way of overcoming prey many times their size.
Beyond the reefs lie immense plains of sand and mud. Here, humpback whales arrive after epic migrations from Antarctica. For one female, this will be her final journey. As she takes her last breath, hundreds of sharks gather nearby. In death, her body becomes a vital source of nutrients, feeding a host of scavengers and bringing life to one of the tropical seas' most barren landscapes.

programme.title: Great Coastal Railway Journeys
programme.desc:
An epic stretch of Scottish coastline is the first stop for Michael Portillo as he begins a series of coastal railway journeys around the British Isles.
Siccar Point, close to Dunbar on the Firth of Forth, was the site of an extraordinary 18th-century discovery and is today a place of pilgrimage for earth scientists from across the world. Michael finds out how James Hutton’s Unconformity upended biblical teaching about the age of the earth.
From North Berwick, Michael takes a boat a mile out into the Firth to visit one of the wildlife wonders of the world, a volcanic island known as Bass Rock. Long since abandoned by humans, it is now a breeding ground for 150,000 northern gannets. Standing with his seabird centre guide and with the white-and-yellow birds nesting and courting only feet away, Michael has to pinch himself to believe the scene.
Next stop is the Scottish capital, Edinburgh. Arriving at Britain’s second largest station, Waverley, Michael walks out into the Old Town with its castle and palace linked by the Royal Mile. He climbs to the city’s highest point, Arthur’s Seat, for a paleontologist’s story of settlement in the region from 7,000 years ago. Neither she nor Michael will forget the name of her favourite fossil, which is tattooed on her fingers.
At Holyrood House, the Queen’s official residence in Scotland, Michael visits the scene of a grisly 16th-century murder, which was the stuff of myth in his childhood. Mary Queen of Scots’ secretary, David Rizzio, was murdered by her husband and fellow lords in front of Mary in her private apartments. The palace building, its location and the historical events that took place within its walls help Michael to understand how royal power continues to be asserted in Scotland. Presenter - Michael Portillo Director - Ben Rowland Series Editor - Alison Kreps Executive Producer - John Comerford Production Company - Fremantle.

programme.title: Escaping Idi Amin
programme.desc:
In September 1972, one month after dictator Idi Amin announces his plan to expel all Ugandan Asians from the country, 80,000 people are making plans to flee, in fear for their lives. Maz and Bharti head for the capital Kampala, where hundreds gather, desperate to find out whether their British passports will be enough to escape to Britain.
As the deadline approaches, Harminder’s father escapes arrest and schoolboy Paresh hides during overnight curfews while gunfire echoes across the city.
Britain is divided. Controversial politician Enoch Powell rallies those who say the Ugandan Asians have no right to come, a newspaper poll finds just six per cent of the public want them here, and some councils try to steer new arrivals away from their cities.
In Uganda, Amin refuses to negotiate – stepping up the pressure on those stuck in the country. programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc:
Four familiar faces paired with a friend or a loved one leave their luxury lifestyles at the starting line for a journey that will take them to the other side of the world and push them to the limits of their endurance. The pairs embark on a life-changing adventure - a 7,500km race from the prehistoric jungles of Borneo to the sun-baked southern tip of Australia.
Competing in this series are acclaimed singer-songwriter and musician Sam Ryder, and his best friend and tour manager, Kaz; veteran sports broadcaster Jeff Stelling and his son Matt; BRIT award-winning singer-songwriter Ella Eyre and childhood friend Nana; and influencer Princess Andre with her brother musician Junior Andre.
Stripped of their smartphones and bank cards, these household names will be tested; emotions will run high, and relationships will be transformed on an adventure that’s as challenging as it is rewarding. They will need to rely on their own resourcefulness and the kindness of strangers to reach the finish line, equipped with only a map and a budget of £26 each a day.
Their race begins in Kuching, a vibrant city in north west Malaysian Borneo and the gateway to the island's vast wilderness. From there, the teams must cross three countries and two continents, weaving through five checkpoints before reaching the finish line in Melbourne, Australia.
The teams must tackle the most formidable race yet - traversing the ancient jungles and indigenous heartlands of Borneo, navigating the Makassar Strait to Sulawesi, an island of cinematic, towering limestone cliffs, before reaching the kaleidoscopic splendour of Queensland's landscapes, from the turquoise blues of the Great Barrier Reef to the arid, expansive orange of the outback. Finally, they will thread through sprawling Sydney before reaching the finish line on the southern tip of Australia.
Musician Sam and tour manager Kaz embrace an unexpected start to the race and dive straight in, relishing the chance to revisit the early days of their friendship when roughing it on tour was the norm. They undertake a jungle adventure, heading inland to connect with the indigenous Tae people.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are
programme.desc: Actor and writer Ruth Jones - Nessa from Gavin and Stacey - investigates her Welsh family’s history. On her mum’s side, she discovers that her great-great-great-grandfather was a mariner who rose to the rank of captain in the domestic coastal trade. His son surpassed his father by carrying Welsh coal across the world. On Ruth’s dad’s side, she looks into the career of the grandfather she never met. Henry Richard Jones was a leading light in the Medical Aid Societies of south Wales, which provided a model for the National Health Service in 1948. Only two contestants will make it to the cash builder and the chance to double their combined cash before the dramatic final, where they must make the ultimate decision. programme.desc:
First through the door today is mystical Claire. The oddity of her quirky crystal ball augurs well, but is it desirable enough to help her find a fortune?
Next up facing the dealers are Sally and Linda from Durham, with a range of medical posters their dad rescued from a skip. Condition will be key, so what will valuation expert Simon Bower’s diagnosis be?
Third to try to make a sale is wheeler dealer Greg, with a chest he believes came from a historic White Star ocean liner. Objects associated with the Titanic and its sister ships are always of interest, but they need perfect provenance if they’re going to make a tidy profit.
Unlike Greg, Samantha can guarantee her offering is authentic: a letter sent to her by Mother Teresa after they met at an awards ceremony. It’s the type of lot Simon usually advises should be put into a specialist auction, but will any of the dealers be tempted to make her an offer?
And last but not least, in what initially sounds like a follow-up to one of Dickens’s finest works, it’s a tale of two Nigels in the valuation room. programme.desc:
Christina Trevanion goes underground to explore medieval passageways beneath Exeter city centre. In the company of historian Professor Mark Stoyle, she learns how 425 metres of tunnels were built over water pipes to bring clean water to the city’s people in the 1300s.
Above ground, four teams shop for treasures at a huge antiques fair on the outskirts of Exeter. The red teams are firefighters Steve and Andrew, and friends Tricia and Debbie, all skippered by expert Richard Madley. Their opponents in blue are sales assistants Jack and Shaun, and friends Tony and Danny, guided by expert Ben Cooper.
A flock of geese decoys stops Steve and Andrew in their tracks, but the price is sky high, so they walk on by. Meanwhile, Tony and Danny spot a set of bagpipes, but it’s too much of a squeeze on their budget.
With their shopping bags full, the teams travel to nearby Hele in north Devon, where auctioneer Adam Partridge is on the rostrum selling them to the highest bidder.

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
When an exclusive, high-roller poker night ends with the murder of oil magnate and seemingly devoted family man Jeremy Hare, Rose and Raj find themselves completely out of their depth in the gambling world. The evidence is perplexing. Jeremy’s substantial winnings from the night are still on his body, and he’s been stabbed with an ornate, ceremonial golden knife that was left at the scene. Unfamiliar with the complex strategies and unspoken rules of high-stakes poker, Rose and Raj are left struggling to decipher the various hidden motives of the players around the table.
The game was hosted by Ace Dawso, a slick operator and local villain, with whom Joe and Rose have had a previous run-in. Ace’s invitation-only matches attract an elite, ruthless crowd. There’s Rami Ashraf, an enigmatic Egyptian playboy and seasoned poker pro with secrets to protect; Eleanor Calvert, a sharp stock-market whiz and one of the country’s wealthiest, most calculating women; and Ace himself, who sat out the fatal hand but oversaw the room with a watchful eye. Every player present had something to lose and possibly a reason to want Jeremy silenced.
Baffled by the tight-lipped suspects who can quickly tell that she doesn’t understand the game, Rose soon realises that conventional police work won't crack this case. She has no choice but to recruit Joe, whose history makes him the ultimate insider. Enticed back into the illicit world of gambling, Joe is forced to confront the dangerous addiction that nearly ruined his life. To help Rose read the table and flush out a cold-blooded killer, Joe must walk a risky tightrope, gambling not just with cash, but with his own addictions.

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
On All Saints’ Day, Pam Rhodes celebrates the life of St Francis of Assisi 800 years since his death and meets Christians still inspired by his teachings.
St Francis is one of the most well-known figures in Christian history. Famous for his profound love of nature, he is the patron saint of ecology and animals, and this year has been designated by Pope Leo XIV as a Franciscan jubilee year. Pam Rhodes explores how he has inspired others to follow in his footsteps and how his legacy of faith and care lives on.
In Liverpool, Pam meets Fr Maximilian Martin at St Anthony of Padua Friary to discover what it means to live as a Franciscan friar. He found his calling after ten years as a nurse, and he shares the timeless message of St Francis - simplicity, caring for creation and serving the vulnerable - while offering a glimpse into a life of poverty, chastity and obedience right in the heart of the local community.
In Salford, we visit the Laudato Si' Centre at Wardley Hall, the diocese's ambitious response to Pope Francis’s call to care for our common home. Environment and learning officer Emily Cahill leads a group of students from St Ambrose Barlow RC Secondary School on a retreat day. Getting their hands in the soil, the students discover the beauty of nature first-hand and learn how to become the next generation of guardians of creation.
Finally, Pam heads to Birkenhead to meet Steph Worsley, a dedicated veterinary nurse with nearly 27 years of experience. Raised in a Methodist farming community, Steph proudly wears the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons badge, which features St Francis at its centre as a daily reminder of her professional oath to respect and protect all animals.
1. For All the Saints - Chester Cathedral2. Make Me a Channel of Your Peace – St George’s RC Cathedral, Southwark 3. Way Maker - Gas Street Church, Birmingham4. Spirit and Truth - The Monastery, Manchester5. All Creatures of Our God and King - Our Lady's Church, York6. programme.title: Blue Planet II
programme.desc:
In recent years, our knowledge of life beneath the waves has been transformed. Using cutting-edge technology in this extended special, we celebrate the highlights from the series. From the intense heat of the tropics to our planet's frozen poles, through to its unexplored depths, we reveal new worlds and extraordinary, never-seen-before animal behaviours.
Starting in the tropical coral reefs - the most diverse ocean habitat - a tusk fish demonstrates a surprising level of ingenuity using corals as an anvil to break open clams. In the Seychelles, half a million terns nest on an island. Fledglings must eventually take to the wing, but danger lurks beneath the waves: metre-long giant trevally fish leap clear out of the water to snatch birds.
In the tropics, the sun heats the sea, creating rain, winds and huge storms that drive up towards higher latitudes. Here, the seas change with the seasons. In spring, thousands of mobula rays gather in Mexico's Sea of Cortez. At night, in a previously unseen event, tiny organisms that light up when disturbed react to their wingbeats, creating an enchanting bioluminescent firework display.
The seasonal seas are home to bountiful kelp forests. In the undersea forests of southern Africa, one resident - the common octopus - has become the ultimate escape artist. To outwit her nemesis, the pyjama shark, she uses ingenious tactics, never filmed before.
On the coast, two worlds collide. Where sea meets land, coasts are the most dynamic and challenging habitats in the ocean. The ever-changing tides create rock pools. But these temporary worlds are a battleground. Predatory starfish turn a magical garden into the stuff of nightmares.
The big blue is the world's greatest wilderness - a vast marine desert where there is little to eat and nowhere to hide. Sometimes, there is a brief explosion of food, but ocean hunters must be fast to make the best of this bonanza. We witness super-pods of up to 5,000 spinner dolphins racing to herd vast shoals of lanternfish, briefly caught at the surface where it is thought they spawn. New aerial footage reveals, for the first time, the spectacular feeding frenzy of 90kg tuna and dolphins smashing through the lantern fish shoals, turning the sea white with foam.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The warm, sunlit waters of the tropics support the greatest diversity of life in the ocean. Bathed in year-round sunlight for millions of years, these seas are home to more species than anywhere else on earth. In a world where competition is fierce, animals have evolved extraordinary ways to survive. Yet even in these seemingly familiar waters, remarkable new behaviours are still being discovered.
At the northern tip of Australia, a tawny nurse shark patrols the shallows in search of food. Too slow to chase fish in open water, it relies on a surprising strategy. Gathering in groups, the sharks appear to work together in a coordinated ambush. After waiting patiently in the shallows, they drive huge shoals of fish out of the water and onto the beach before vacuuming up their prey by the mouthful.
Further west, Shark Bay is home to one of the world's greatest concentrations of dolphins. Here, bottlenose dolphins have developed a hunting technique previously unknown to science. Carrying sea sponges to isolated coral bommies, they use them to block the hiding places of fish, creating one of the most sophisticated examples of trap-setting ever documented in the animal kingdom.
Across the tropics, coral reefs are bustling underwater cities where predators and prey are locked in a constant battle. In the Red Sea, coral groupers communicate with two very different hunting partners - giant Maori wrasse and sleek moray eels. Only by working together can they flush prey from the reef's maze of crevices, making the grouper far more successful than it could ever be alone. After dark in Bali, the reefs take a more sinister turn as harlequin shrimp stalk starfish for supper. Barely five centimetres long, these tiny hunters have developed a macabre way of overcoming prey many times their size.
Beyond the reefs lie immense plains of sand and mud. Here, humpback whales arrive after epic migrations from Antarctica. For one female, this will be her final journey. As she takes her last breath, hundreds of sharks gather nearby. In death, her body becomes a vital source of nutrients, feeding a host of scavengers and bringing life to one of the tropical seas' most barren landscapes.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc:
The story of Iranians who have lived through the most turbulent and traumatic of years, with widespread street protests, a brutal crackdown by the authorities and a war launched against Iran by the US and Israel.
The film follows one mother who begins the year planning a future with her daughter, only to see it end with a promise to avenge her daughter’s death. After she publicly blamed the Iranian authorities, she was forced to flee the country and live in exile.
A medic reveals how his life has changed after treating hundreds of protesters, many with gunshot wounds, while a man who also fled Iran in fear shares the last messages from a relative, sentenced to death.
Filmed both inside and outside the country, this is the raw and uncompromising story of a year in Iran, told by some of the people who were there. programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc:
Four familiar faces paired with a friend or a loved one leave their luxury lifestyles at the starting line for a journey that will take them to the other side of the world and push them to the limits of their endurance. The pairs embark on a life-changing adventure - a 7,500km race from the prehistoric jungles of Borneo to the sun-baked southern tip of Australia.
Competing in this series are acclaimed singer-songwriter and musician Sam Ryder, and his best friend and tour manager, Kaz; veteran sports broadcaster Jeff Stelling and his son Matt; BRIT award-winning singer-songwriter Ella Eyre and childhood friend Nana; and influencer Princess Andre with her brother musician Junior Andre.
Stripped of their smartphones and bank cards, these household names will be tested; emotions will run high, and relationships will be transformed on an adventure that’s as challenging as it is rewarding. They will need to rely on their own resourcefulness and the kindness of strangers to reach the finish line, equipped with only a map and a budget of £26 each a day.
Their race begins in Kuching, a vibrant city in north west Malaysian Borneo and the gateway to the island's vast wilderness. From there, the teams must cross three countries and two continents, weaving through five checkpoints before reaching the finish line in Melbourne, Australia.
The teams must tackle the most formidable race yet - traversing the ancient jungles and indigenous heartlands of Borneo, navigating the Makassar Strait to Sulawesi, an island of cinematic, towering limestone cliffs, before reaching the kaleidoscopic splendour of Queensland's landscapes, from the turquoise blues of the Great Barrier Reef to the arid, expansive orange of the outback. Finally, they will thread through sprawling Sydney before reaching the finish line on the southern tip of Australia.
Musician Sam and tour manager Kaz embrace an unexpected start to the race and dive straight in, relishing the chance to revisit the early days of their friendship when roughing it on tour was the norm. They undertake a jungle adventure, heading inland to connect with the indigenous Tae people.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are
programme.desc: Actor and writer Ruth Jones - Nessa from Gavin and Stacey - investigates her Welsh family’s history. On her mum’s side, she discovers that her great-great-great-grandfather was a mariner who rose to the rank of captain in the domestic coastal trade. His son surpassed his father by carrying Welsh coal across the world. On Ruth’s dad’s side, she looks into the career of the grandfather she never met. Henry Richard Jones was a leading light in the Medical Aid Societies of south Wales, which provided a model for the National Health Service in 1948. programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
When an exclusive, high-roller poker night ends with the murder of oil magnate and seemingly devoted family man Jeremy Hare, Rose and Raj find themselves completely out of their depth in the gambling world. The evidence is perplexing. Jeremy’s substantial winnings from the night are still on his body, and he’s been stabbed with an ornate, ceremonial golden knife that was left at the scene. Unfamiliar with the complex strategies and unspoken rules of high-stakes poker, Rose and Raj are left struggling to decipher the various hidden motives of the players around the table.
The game was hosted by Ace Dawso, a slick operator and local villain, with whom Joe and Rose have had a previous run-in. Ace’s invitation-only matches attract an elite, ruthless crowd. There’s Rami Ashraf, an enigmatic Egyptian playboy and seasoned poker pro with secrets to protect; Eleanor Calvert, a sharp stock-market whiz and one of the country’s wealthiest, most calculating women; and Ace himself, who sat out the fatal hand but oversaw the room with a watchful eye. Every player present had something to lose and possibly a reason to want Jeremy silenced.
Baffled by the tight-lipped suspects who can quickly tell that she doesn’t understand the game, Rose soon realises that conventional police work won't crack this case. She has no choice but to recruit Joe, whose history makes him the ultimate insider. Enticed back into the illicit world of gambling, Joe is forced to confront the dangerous addiction that nearly ruined his life. To help Rose read the table and flush out a cold-blooded killer, Joe must walk a risky tightrope, gambling not just with cash, but with his own addictions.

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
On All Saints’ Day, Pam Rhodes celebrates the life of St Francis of Assisi 800 years since his death and meets Christians still inspired by his teachings.
St Francis is one of the most well-known figures in Christian history. Famous for his profound love of nature, he is the patron saint of ecology and animals, and this year has been designated by Pope Leo XIV as a Franciscan jubilee year. Pam Rhodes explores how he has inspired others to follow in his footsteps and how his legacy of faith and care lives on.
In Liverpool, Pam meets Fr Maximilian Martin at St Anthony of Padua Friary to discover what it means to live as a Franciscan friar. He found his calling after ten years as a nurse, and he shares the timeless message of St Francis - simplicity, caring for creation and serving the vulnerable - while offering a glimpse into a life of poverty, chastity and obedience right in the heart of the local community.
In Salford, we visit the Laudato Si' Centre at Wardley Hall, the diocese's ambitious response to Pope Francis’s call to care for our common home. Environment and learning officer Emily Cahill leads a group of students from St Ambrose Barlow RC Secondary School on a retreat day. Getting their hands in the soil, the students discover the beauty of nature first-hand and learn how to become the next generation of guardians of creation.
Finally, Pam heads to Birkenhead to meet Steph Worsley, a dedicated veterinary nurse with nearly 27 years of experience. Raised in a Methodist farming community, Steph proudly wears the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons badge, which features St Francis at its centre as a daily reminder of her professional oath to respect and protect all animals.
1. For All the Saints - Chester Cathedral2. Make Me a Channel of Your Peace – St George’s RC Cathedral, Southwark 3. Way Maker - Gas Street Church, Birmingham4. Spirit and Truth - The Monastery, Manchester5. All Creatures of Our God and King - Our Lady's Church, York6. programme.title: Blue Planet II
programme.desc:
In recent years, our knowledge of life beneath the waves has been transformed. Using cutting-edge technology in this extended special, we celebrate the highlights from the series. From the intense heat of the tropics to our planet's frozen poles, through to its unexplored depths, we reveal new worlds and extraordinary, never-seen-before animal behaviours.
Starting in the tropical coral reefs - the most diverse ocean habitat - a tusk fish demonstrates a surprising level of ingenuity using corals as an anvil to break open clams. In the Seychelles, half a million terns nest on an island. Fledglings must eventually take to the wing, but danger lurks beneath the waves: metre-long giant trevally fish leap clear out of the water to snatch birds.
In the tropics, the sun heats the sea, creating rain, winds and huge storms that drive up towards higher latitudes. Here, the seas change with the seasons. In spring, thousands of mobula rays gather in Mexico's Sea of Cortez. At night, in a previously unseen event, tiny organisms that light up when disturbed react to their wingbeats, creating an enchanting bioluminescent firework display.
The seasonal seas are home to bountiful kelp forests. In the undersea forests of southern Africa, one resident - the common octopus - has become the ultimate escape artist. To outwit her nemesis, the pyjama shark, she uses ingenious tactics, never filmed before.
On the coast, two worlds collide. Where sea meets land, coasts are the most dynamic and challenging habitats in the ocean. The ever-changing tides create rock pools. But these temporary worlds are a battleground. Predatory starfish turn a magical garden into the stuff of nightmares.
The big blue is the world's greatest wilderness - a vast marine desert where there is little to eat and nowhere to hide. Sometimes, there is a brief explosion of food, but ocean hunters must be fast to make the best of this bonanza. We witness super-pods of up to 5,000 spinner dolphins racing to herd vast shoals of lanternfish, briefly caught at the surface where it is thought they spawn. New aerial footage reveals, for the first time, the spectacular feeding frenzy of 90kg tuna and dolphins smashing through the lantern fish shoals, turning the sea white with foam.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The warm, sunlit waters of the tropics support the greatest diversity of life in the ocean. Bathed in year-round sunlight for millions of years, these seas are home to more species than anywhere else on earth. In a world where competition is fierce, animals have evolved extraordinary ways to survive. Yet even in these seemingly familiar waters, remarkable new behaviours are still being discovered.
At the northern tip of Australia, a tawny nurse shark patrols the shallows in search of food. Too slow to chase fish in open water, it relies on a surprising strategy. Gathering in groups, the sharks appear to work together in a coordinated ambush. After waiting patiently in the shallows, they drive huge shoals of fish out of the water and onto the beach before vacuuming up their prey by the mouthful.
Further west, Shark Bay is home to one of the world's greatest concentrations of dolphins. Here, bottlenose dolphins have developed a hunting technique previously unknown to science. Carrying sea sponges to isolated coral bommies, they use them to block the hiding places of fish, creating one of the most sophisticated examples of trap-setting ever documented in the animal kingdom.
Across the tropics, coral reefs are bustling underwater cities where predators and prey are locked in a constant battle. In the Red Sea, coral groupers communicate with two very different hunting partners - giant Maori wrasse and sleek moray eels. Only by working together can they flush prey from the reef's maze of crevices, making the grouper far more successful than it could ever be alone. After dark in Bali, the reefs take a more sinister turn as harlequin shrimp stalk starfish for supper. Barely five centimetres long, these tiny hunters have developed a macabre way of overcoming prey many times their size.
Beyond the reefs lie immense plains of sand and mud. Here, humpback whales arrive after epic migrations from Antarctica. For one female, this will be her final journey. As she takes her last breath, hundreds of sharks gather nearby. In death, her body becomes a vital source of nutrients, feeding a host of scavengers and bringing life to one of the tropical seas' most barren landscapes.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc:
The story of Iranians who have lived through the most turbulent and traumatic of years, with widespread street protests, a brutal crackdown by the authorities and a war launched against Iran by the US and Israel.
The film follows one mother who begins the year planning a future with her daughter, only to see it end with a promise to avenge her daughter’s death. After she publicly blamed the Iranian authorities, she was forced to flee the country and live in exile.
A medic reveals how his life has changed after treating hundreds of protesters, many with gunshot wounds, while a man who also fled Iran in fear shares the last messages from a relative, sentenced to death.
Filmed both inside and outside the country, this is the raw and uncompromising story of a year in Iran, told by some of the people who were there. programme.title: Property Brothers: Buying and Selling
programme.desc: In the fifth season, more couples put their homes in the bros' hands. Can Jonathan and Drew raise the roof off of dilapidated, draughty and dingy digs?Adina and Trey are in a race against time to sell their house before a subdivision floods the market with1000 new homes. But can authoritative Adina relinquish control to the twins?

programme.title: Undercover Boss USA
programme.desc: Clean Harbours is a hazardous waste disposal company, dealing with everything from hurricanes and oil spills to the 9/11 clean-up operation. Its chairman and founder Alan McKim is struggling to avoid losing highly trained employees as the business expands, so he goes undercover as a mechanic to discover the reason why.

programme.title: Couples Come Dine with Me
programme.sub-title: S2E14 ║ Essex and East London ║ Cooking, Leisure Hobbies
programme.desc: Three rival couples in Essex and east London compete in the dinner-party challenge, beginning with Spencer and Sara's simple Jewish feast. Reserved pair Lauren and Jack prepare a sophisticated menu reflecting the hosts' heritage in South Africa and Burma. For the final dinner, Paul and Ed opt for a flavourful fare that proves a bit much for those with a fondness for plainer food, and with the contest over, the competitors anxiously wait to discover which party was considered the best.

programme.title: Couples Come Dine with Me
programme.sub-title: S2E7 ║ East London ║ Cooking, Leisure Hobbies
programme.desc: Three pairs of partners from east London compete to win the £1,000 prize, including Stephen and Andrew who present a cosy menu inspired by their love of all things homely. Also vying to win are beauty-lovers Rob and Abi who hope to impress their guests by cooking up some glamorous cuisine, before comedian duo James and Kate hope a surprise performance will help them secure the cash.

programme.title: Couples Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: Three couples in Luton, Bedfordshire, battle it out in the culinary contest, beginning with Bridget and her husband Peter, whose menu of tried and tested dinner party favourites leaves their rivals distinctly unimpressed. Next to host are Shawn and Kendra, who prepare dishes based on their travels, before serving up a dessert that reflects their Canadian heritage. Finally, footballer Richard and his fiancee Marina decide to cook an Italian-inspired meal - but Richard proves to be more of a hindrance than a help in the kitchen. With the trio of parties complete, the couples reconvene to decide which pair hosted the best event.

programme.title: Ramsay's Kitchen Nightmares USA
programme.sub-title: S4E13 ║ Mojito, the Junction and Bazzini ║ Cooking, Leisure Hobbies
programme.desc: In this revisit episode, chef Gordon Ramsay goes back to Mojito, the Junction (formerly known as Flamangos) and Bazzini to check in with the owners he helped in the past and find out whether his advice has been put to good use. Will he be pleased with their progress?

programme.title: Ramsay's Kitchen Nightmares USA
programme.desc: The chef heads to floundering soul food restaurant Blackberry's in Plainfield, New Jersey, but struggles to get his message across to indomitable owner Shelley. Her refusal to deal with the truth comes to a head when Gordon finds a dead mouse in the doorway, prompting him to step up his efforts to change her ways.

programme.title: Ramsay's Kitchen Nightmares USA
programme.desc: Gordon Ramsay is in New Jersey to help Rose Leone, who spent two years in a coma and came out of hospital to learn her son Michael had run her once-thriving Italian restaurant into the ground. With a menu of more than 126 dishes, the quality of the food is suffering, and even the chefs refuse to eat their own creations.

programme.title: Ramsay's Kitchen Nightmares USA
programme.sub-title: S5E3 ║ Burger Kitchen - Part One ║ Cooking, Leisure Hobbies
programme.desc: First of a two-part special in which Gordon Ramsay heads to the Burger Kitchen in Los Angeles, where tensions are running high because owner Alan Saffron has spent his son's entire inheritance on the struggling restaurant. To make matters worse, the kitchen is run by a chef called David Blaine who shares nothing of his famous namesake's magic when it comes to cooking - and whose threatening behaviour regularly gets him into trouble.

programme.title: Ramsay's Kitchen Nightmares USA

Alan gets a wake-up call from internet critics, who he believes are trying to shut him down.

Among the competitors still in with a shout of becoming champion, Nina Conti repeatedly insults a citrus fruit, Chloe Petts struggles to light a match, Isy Suttie focuses intently on the year 1991 and Matt Lucas bravely decides to cut Greg Davies down to size.
